questions.stem: X is a crystalline salt of sodium. A solution of X in water turns litmus red and produces a gas which turns lime water milky when added to sodium carbonate. With barium chloride solution, X gives a white precipitate which is insoluble in dilute hydrochloric acid. X is
questions.explanation: X is an acid salt (turns litmus red, liberates CO2 from carbonate) and a sulphate (BaSO4 insoluble in dilute HCl), so it is NaHSO4.

questions.stem: The alkanol obtained from the production of soap is
questions.explanation: Saponification of fats/oils with alkali gives soap and glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol).

questions.stem: The flame used by welders in cutting metals is
questions.explanation: Ethyne burnt in oxygen (oxy-acetylene flame) gives a very hot flame (about 3000 °C) used for cutting and welding metals.

questions.stem: Consecutive members of an alkane homologous series differ by
questions.explanation: Successive members of any homologous series differ by a -CH2- unit.

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: If an element has the electronic configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p2, it is
questions.explanation: The last electrons enter a 3p orbital, so the element (silicon) is a p-block element.

questions.stem: Some copper (II) sulphate pentahydrate (CuSO4.5H2O) was heated at 120 °C with the following results: Wt of crucible = 10.00 g; Wt of crucible + CuSO4.5H2O = 14.98 g; Wt of crucible + residue = 13.54 g. How many molecules of water of crystallization were lost? [H = 1, Cu = 63.5, O = 16, S = 32]
questions.explanation: Moles of hydrate = 4.98/249.5 = 0.020; water lost = 1.44 g = 0.080 mol; 0.080/0.020 = 4 molecules lost.

questions.stem: The three-dimensional shape of methane is
questions.explanation: Carbon in methane uses four sp3 bonding pairs, giving a tetrahedral shape (bond angle 109.5°).

questions.stem:
An unknown organic compound X has a relative molecular mass of 180. It is a colourless crystalline solid, readily soluble in water. X contains the elements C, H and O in the atomic ratio 1:2:1. The compound has a sweet taste and melts on heating. In the presence of yeast and in the absence of air, X is converted to compound Y and a colourless gas. Compound Y reacts with sodium metal to produce a gas Z which gives a 'pop' sound with a glowing splint. Y also reacts with ethanoic acid to give a sweet-smelling compound W.
Compound W is
questions.explanation: X is glucose, Y is ethanol; ethanol + ethanoic acid gives the sweet-smelling ester ethyl ethanoate.

questions.stem:
An unknown organic compound X has a relative molecular mass of 180. It is a colourless crystalline solid, readily soluble in water. X contains the elements C, H and O in the atomic ratio 1:2:1. The compound has a sweet taste and melts on heating. In the presence of yeast and in the absence of air, X is converted to compound Y and a colourless gas. Compound Y reacts with sodium metal to produce a gas Z which gives a 'pop' sound with a glowing splint. Y also reacts with ethanoic acid to give a sweet-smelling compound W.
The molecular formula of X is
questions.explanation: Empirical formula CH2O (30); 180/30 = 6, so X is C6H12O6.

questions.stem:
An unknown organic compound X has a relative molecular mass of 180. It is a colourless crystalline solid, readily soluble in water. X contains the elements C, H and O in the atomic ratio 1:2:1. The compound has a sweet taste and melts on heating. In the presence of yeast and in the absence of air, X is converted to compound Y and a colourless gas. Compound Y reacts with sodium metal to produce a gas Z which gives a 'pop' sound with a glowing splint. Y also reacts with ethanoic acid to give a sweet-smelling compound W.
The reaction of X with yeast forms the basis of the
questions.explanation: Fermentation of glucose by yeast to ethanol and CO2 is the basis of brewing.

questions.stem: A mixture of common salt, ammonium chloride and barium sulphate can best be separated by
options: addition of water followed by filtration then sublimation
addition of water followed by sublimation then filtration
sublimation followed by addition of water then filtration
questions.explanation: Sublime off NH4Cl first, then add water to dissolve the salt and filter off insoluble BaSO4.

questions.stem: Which of the following relationships between the pressure P, the volume V and the temperature T represents ideal gas behaviour?
questions.explanation: For an ideal gas PV = nRT, so P ∝ T/V.

questions.stem: The colour imparted to a flame by calcium ion is
questions.explanation: Calcium ions give a brick-red flame.

questions.stem:
In which of the following processes is iron being oxidized?
1. Fe + H2SO4 → H2 + FeSO4
2. FeSO4 + H2S → FeS + H2SO4
3. 2FeCl2 + Cl2 → 2FeCl3
4. 2FeCl3 + SnCl2 → 2FeCl2 + SnCl4
questions.explanation: Iron's oxidation number rises in 1 (0 → +2) and 3 (+2 → +3); it is unchanged in 2 and falls in 4.

questions.stem: In the experiment (Fig. 2: CuSO4 and AgNO3 cells connected in series), a current was passed for 10 minutes and 0.63 g of copper was found to be deposited on the cathode of the CuSO4 cell. The weight of silver deposited in the AgNO3 cell during the same period would be [Cu = 63, Ag = 108]
questions.explanation: 0.63/63 = 0.01 mol Cu needs 0.02 mol electrons, which deposit 0.02 mol Ag = 2.16 g.

questions.stem: In the reaction Fe + Cu2+ → Fe2+ + Cu, iron displaces copper ions to form copper. This is due to the fact that
options: iron is in the metallic form while the copper is in the ionic form
the atomic weight of copper is greater than that of iron
copper metal has more electrons than iron metal
iron is higher in the electrochemical series than copper
questions.explanation: A metal higher in the electrochemical series displaces a lower one from solution of its ions.

questions.stem: How many isomeric forms are there for the molecular formula C3H6Br2?
questions.explanation: 1,1-, 1,2-, 1,3- and 2,2-dibromopropane: four isomers.

questions.stem: A piece of burning sulphur will continue to burn in a gas jar of oxygen to give misty fumes which readily dissolve in water. The resulting liquid is
questions.explanation: Sulphur burns to SO2, which dissolves in water to form H2SO3, trioxosulphate (IV) acid.

questions.stem: Sodium sulphate decahydrate (Na2SO4.10H2O) on exposure to air loses all its water of crystallization. The process of loss is known as
questions.explanation: Loss of water of crystallization to the atmosphere on exposure is efflorescence.

questions.stem: Which of the following happens during the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride?
questions.explanation: At the anode Cl- loses electrons to form Cl2, i.e. chloride ion is oxidized.

questions.stem: Crude petroleum pollutant usually seen on some Nigerian creeks and waterways can be dispersed or removed by
options: heating the affected parts in order to boil off the petroleum
mechanically stirring to dissolve the petroleum in water
pouring organic solvents to dissolve the petroleum
cooling to freeze out the petroleum
questions.explanation: Detergents emulsify and disperse oil spills on water.

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: An element is electronegative if
options: it has a tendency to exist in the gaseous form
its ions dissolve readily in water
it has a tendency to lose electrons
it has a tendency to gain electrons
questions.explanation: Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom to attract/gain electrons.

questions.stem: Solutions X, Y and Z have pH values 3.0, 5.0 and 9.0 respectively. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Y and Z are more acidic than water
Y is more acidic than X
questions.explanation: Z (pH 9) is alkaline, hence the least acidic of the three.

questions.stem:
In the reactions
(I) H2(g) + 1/2 O2(g) → H2O(l); ΔH = -2.86 kJ
(II) C(s) + O2(g) → CO2(g); ΔH = -406 kJ
the equations imply that
questions.explanation: Both are exothermic; reaction (I) releases less heat (smaller magnitude of ΔH). ΔH says nothing about rate.

questions.stem: Stainless steel is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Stainless steel is iron with carbon and chromium (often nickel).

questions.stem: What volume of 0.50 M H2SO4 will exactly neutralize 20 cm3 of 0.1 M NaOH solution?
questions.explanation: Moles NaOH = 0.002; H2SO4 needed = 0.001 mol; V = 0.001/0.50 dm3 = 2.0 cm3.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of gases will NOT react further with oxygen at a temperature between 30 °C and 400 °C?
questions.explanation: NO2 and SO3 are already in their highest common oxidation states; the other pairs each contain a gas (SO2, NH3, H2, NO, CO) that can be further oxidized.

questions.stem: Some metals are extracted from their ores after some preliminary treatments by electrolysis (L), some by thermal reaction (T) and some by a combination of both processes (TL). Which set-up in the following for the extraction of iron, copper and aluminium is correct?
questions.explanation: Iron is reduced thermally in the blast furnace; aluminium needs purification of bauxite and then electrolysis of fused alumina.

questions.stem: In the preparation of some pure crystals of Cu(NO3)2 starting with CuO, a student gave the following statements as steps he employed. Which of these shows a flaw in his report?
options: Some CuO was reacted with excess dilute H2SO4
When the concentrate was cooled, crystals formed were removed by filtration
The crystals were washed with very cold water
The crystals were then allowed to dry
questions.explanation: To obtain copper(II) nitrate, CuO must be reacted with dilute HNO3, not H2SO4 (which gives CuSO4).

questions.stem: Which of the following separation processes is most likely to yield high quality ethanol (>95%) from palm wine?
questions.explanation: Fractional distillation concentrates ethanol and a dehydrant (e.g. CaO) removes the remaining water.

questions.stem: Increasing the pressure of a gas
options: lowers the average kinetic energy of the molecules
decreases the density of the gas
decreases the temperature of the gas
increases the density of the gas
increases the volume of the gas
questions.explanation: Higher pressure compresses the gas into a smaller volume, so its density increases.

questions.stem: 2.5 g of a hydrated barium salt gave, on heating, 2.13 g of the anhydrous salt. Given that the relative molecular mass of the anhydrous salt is 208, the number of molecules of water of crystallization of the barium salt is
questions.explanation: Anhydrous: 2.13/208 = 0.0102 mol; water: 0.37/18 = 0.0206 mol; ratio = 2.

questions.stem: 3.06 g of a sample of potassium trioxochlorate (V) (KClO3) was required to make a saturated solution with 10 cm3 of water at 25 °C. The solubility of the salt at 25 °C is [K = 39, Cl = 35.5, O = 16]
The cracking process is very important in the petroleum industry because it
questions.explanation: Cracking breaks heavy fractions into lighter ones such as petrol, increasing the yield of engine fuels.

questions.stem: A gas that can behave as a reducing agent towards chlorine and as an oxidizing agent towards hydrogen sulphide is
questions.explanation: SO2 reduces Cl2 (in water) and oxidizes H2S to sulphur.

questions.stem: Which of the following solutions will give a white precipitate with barium chloride solution and a green flame test?
questions.explanation: The sulphate gives white BaSO4 with BaCl2; copper ions give a green flame.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: The mass of an atom is determined by
options: the number of neutrons and protons
the number of neutrons and electrons
questions.explanation: Almost all the mass of an atom is in the nucleus: protons plus neutrons.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a neutralization reaction?
options: Addition of trioxonitrate (V) acid (nitric acid) to distilled water
Addition of trioxonitrate (V) acid (nitric acid) to tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid (sulphuric acid)
Addition of trioxonitrate (V) acid (nitric acid) to potassium hydroxide solution
questions.explanation: An acid reacting with a base (HNO3 + KOH → KNO3 + H2O) is neutralization.

questions.stem: A jet plane carrying 3,000 kg of ethane burns off all the gas forming water and carbon dioxide. If all the carbon dioxide is expelled and the water formed is condensed and kept on board the plane, then the gain in weight is
questions.explanation: C2H6 → 3H2O: 3000/30 = 100 kmol ethane gives 300 kmol water = 5400 kg; net gain = 5400 - 3000 = 2400 kg.

questions.stem: Liquid X reacts with sodium trioxocarbonate (IV) (Na2CO3) to give a gas which turns calcium chloride solution milky. X is
questions.explanation: Acids liberate CO2 from carbonates.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: Copper (II) ion can be reduced to copper (I) ion by hydrochloric acid and zinc
Sodium metal dissolves in water giving oxygen
Carbon dioxide is soluble in water
Lead has a higher atomic weight than copper
questions.explanation: Sodium reacts with water to give hydrogen (and NaOH), not oxygen.

questions.stem: When sodium dioxonitrate (III) (NaNO2) dissolves in water, the process is
questions.explanation: Dissolving sodium dioxonitrate(III) absorbs heat (the solution cools), so it is endothermic.

questions.stem: Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2. The rate of the above reaction will be greatly increased if
options: the zinc is in the powdered form
a greater volume of the acid is used
a smaller volume of the acid is used
the reaction vessel is immersed in an ice-bath
the zinc is in the form of pellets
questions.explanation: Powdering increases the surface area of zinc in contact with acid.

questions.stem: Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2. In the above reaction how much zinc will be left undissolved if 2.00 g of zinc is treated with 10 cm3 of 1.0 M H2SO4? [Zn = 65, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: Acid = 0.010 mol, dissolving 0.010 × 65 = 0.65 g Zn; 2.00 - 0.65 = 1.35 g left.

questions.stem: 30 cm3 of 0.1 M Al(NO3)3 solution is reacted with 100 cm3 of 0.15 M NaOH solution. Which is in excess and by how much?
questions.explanation: Al3+ = 0.003 mol needs 0.009 mol OH- = 60 cm3 of 0.15 M NaOH; 100 - 60 = 40 cm3 NaOH in excess.

questions.stem: Sodium chloride may be obtained from brine by
questions.explanation: Evaporating the water from brine leaves the dissolved sodium chloride.

questions.stem: 20 cm3 of hydrogen gas are sparked with 20 cm3 of oxygen gas in a eudiometer at 373 K (100 °C) and 1 atmosphere. The resulting mixture is cooled to 298 K (25 °C) and passed over calcium chloride. The volume of the residual gas is
questions.explanation: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O: 20 cm3 H2 uses 10 cm3 O2; the water is removed by CaCl2, leaving 10 cm3 of unreacted O2.

questions.stem: For the reaction NH4NO2 → N2 + 2H2O, calculate the volume of nitrogen that would be produced at S.T.P. from 3.20 g of the trioxonitrate (III) salt. (Relative atomic masses: N = 14, O = 16, H = 1)
Which among the elements 1. Carbon 2. Oxygen 3. Copper 4. Bromine 5. Zinc will NOT react with either water or steam?
questions.explanation: Carbon and zinc react with steam and bromine reacts with water; oxygen and copper do not react with water or steam.

questions.stem: Naphthalene when heated melts at 354 K (81 °C). At this temperature the molecules of naphthalene
options: become mobile as the intermolecular forces are broken
questions.explanation: On melting, the molecules gain enough energy to overcome intermolecular forces and move about.

questions.stem: The ratio of the number of molecules in 2 g of hydrogen to that in 16 g of oxygen is
questions.explanation: 2 g H2 = 1 mol; 16 g O2 = 0.5 mol; ratio of molecules = 1 : 0.5 = 2 : 1.

questions.stem: The balanced equation for the reaction of tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid with aluminium hydroxide to give water and aluminium tetraoxosulphate (VI) is
questions.explanation: Correct formulae are H2SO4, Al(OH)3 and Al2(SO4)3; balancing gives 3H2SO4 + 2Al(OH)3 → Al2(SO4)3 + 6H2O.

questions.stem: In which of the following reactions does hydrogen peroxide act as a reducing agent?
questions.explanation: Only in D is H2O2 itself oxidized (to O2) while reducing PbO2 (Pb +4 → +2); elsewhere it oxidizes the other reactant.

questions.stem: For the reaction 2Fe3+ + 2I- → 2Fe2+ + I2, which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: I- is displacing an electron from Fe3+
questions.explanation: Iodide ions lose electrons (-1 → 0) and are oxidized to iodine; Fe3+ is reduced.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods may be used to prepare trioxonitrate (V) acid (nitric acid) in the laboratory?
options: Heating ammonia gas with tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid
Heating ammonium trioxonitrate (V) with tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid
Heating sodium trioxonitrate (V) with tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid
Heating potassium trioxonitrate (V) with calcium hydroxide
Heating a mixture of ammonia gas and oxygen
questions.explanation: In the laboratory, nitric acid is made by heating a nitrate (e.g. NaNO3/KNO3) with concentrated H2SO4 and condensing the vapour.

questions.stem: Lime-water, which is used in the laboratory for the detection of carbon (IV) oxide, is an aqueous solution of
questions.explanation: Lime-water is a saturated solution of calcium hydroxide.

questions.stem: An element that can exist in two or more different structural forms which possess the same chemical properties is said to exhibit
questions.explanation: Different physical forms of the same element in the same state (e.g. diamond and graphite) are allotropes.

questions.stem: Sulphur
options: conducts electricity in the molten state
is usually stored in the form of sticks in water
questions.explanation: Sulphur burns in air with a blue flame forming SO2; its oxides are acidic and it is a non-conductor.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true of carbon monoxide?
options: CO is readily oxidized at room temperature by air to form CO2
CO may be prepared by reducing CO2 with coke heated to about 1000 °C
CO may be prepared by heating charcoal with a limited amount of O2
CO is a good reducing agent
questions.explanation: CO burns in air only when ignited; it is not readily oxidized by air at room temperature.

questions.stem: From the reactions: ZnO + Na2O → Na2ZnO2 and ZnO + CO2 → ZnCO3, it may be concluded that zinc oxide is
questions.explanation: ZnO reacts with a basic oxide (acting as acid) and with an acidic oxide (acting as base), so it is amphoteric.

questions.stem: An example of a neutral oxide is
questions.explanation: CO is neutral; Al2O3 is amphoteric while NO2, CO2 and SO2 are acidic.

questions.stem: 3Cl2 + 2NH3 → N2 + 6HCl. In the above reaction, ammonia acts as
questions.explanation: Nitrogen in NH3 is oxidized from -3 to 0 (N2), so ammonia is the reducing agent.

questions.stem: In the Haber process for the manufacture of ammonia, finely divided iron is used as
questions.explanation: Finely divided iron catalyses N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3.

questions.stem: An organic compound with a vapour density of 56.5 has the following percentage composition: C = 53.1%, N = 12.4%, O = 28.3%, H = 6.2%. The molecular formula of the compound is [C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, H = 1]
When the kerosene fraction from petroleum is heated at high temperature, a lower boiling liquid is obtained. This process is known as
questions.explanation: Breaking large hydrocarbon molecules into smaller, lower-boiling ones by heat is cracking.

questions.stem: CH3-CH2-COOH is
questions.explanation: A three-carbon chain ending in -COOH is propanoic acid.

questions.stem: Alkaline hydrolysis of naturally occurring fats and oils yields
questions.explanation: Saponification of fats/oils by alkali gives soap and glycerol.

questions.stem: Which of the statements is INCORRECT?
options: Fractional distillation of crude petroleum will give the following hydrocarbon fuels in order of increasing boiling point: butane < petrol < kerosene
H2C=CH2 will serve as a monomer in the preparation of polythene
Both but-1-ene and but-1-yne will decolorize bromine readily
But-2-ene will react with chlorine to form 2,3-dichlorobutane
Calcium carbide will react with water to form any alkyne
questions.explanation: Calcium carbide and water give only ethyne, not any alkyne.

questions.stem: If the cost of electricity required to deposit 1 g of magnesium is N5.00, how much would it cost to deposit 10 g of aluminium? (Relative atomic masses: Al = 27, Mg = 24)
questions.explanation: 1 g Mg needs 1/12 F, so 1 F costs N60; 10 g Al needs (10/27) × 3 = 1.11 F, costing N66.67.

questions.stem: Water is said to be 'hard' if it
options: has to be warmed before sodium chloride dissolves in it
forms an insoluble scum with soap
questions.explanation: Hard water contains Ca2+/Mg2+ ions which form an insoluble scum with soap.

questions.stem: Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) pellets are
questions.explanation: NaOH absorbs enough water from the air to dissolve in it, so it is deliquescent.

questions.stem: Alkanes
questions.explanation: Alkanes are hydrocarbons (CnH2n+2) containing only carbon and hydrogen.

questions.stem: If an excess of a liquid hydrocarbon is poured into a jar of chlorine, and the sealed jar is then exposed for several hours to bright sunlight, all the chlorine gas is consumed. The hydrocarbon is said to have undergone
questions.explanation: Slow reaction with chlorine requiring sunlight is typical of photochemical substitution in saturated hydrocarbons.

questions.stem: A piece of sea shell, when dropped into a dilute solution of hydrochloric acid, produces a colourless odourless gas which turns clear limewater milky. The shell contains
questions.explanation: The gas is CO2, liberated from the calcium carbonate in the shell.

questions.stem: An aqueous solution of a metal salt M gives a white precipitate with NaOH, which dissolves in excess NaOH. With aqueous ammonia the solution of M also gives a white precipitate which dissolves in excess ammonia. Therefore the cation in M is
questions.explanation: Zn(OH)2 is white and dissolves in excess of both NaOH and NH3 (forming zincate and tetraamminezinc ions).

questions.stem: The I.U.P.A.C. name for the compound CH3-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH3 is
questions.explanation: The longest chain has four carbons with a methyl on carbon 2 (lowest numbering): 2-methylbutane.

questions.stem: At S.T.P. how many litres of hydrogen can be obtained from the reaction of 500 cm3 of 0.5 M H2SO4 with excess zinc metal? (Gram molecular volume of H2 = 22.4 dm3)
Which of the following conducts electricity?
questions.explanation: Graphite has delocalized (mobile) electrons between its layers, so it conducts electricity.

questions.stem: An organic compound contains 72% carbon, 12% hydrogen and 16% oxygen by mass. The empirical formula of the compound is (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16)
0.499 g of CuSO4.xH2O when heated to constant weight gave a residue of 0.346 g. The value of x is (Cu = 63.5, S = 32.0, O = 16, H = 1)
Hydrogen diffuses through a porous plug
options: at the same rate as oxygen
at a slower rate than oxygen
three times as fast as oxygen
four times as fast as oxygen
questions.explanation: By Graham's law, rate ∝ 1/√M: rate(H2)/rate(O2) = √(32/2) = 4.

questions.stem: Given that the relative atomic mass of iron is 56 and that of oxygen is 16, how many moles of iron (III) oxide will be contained in 1 kg of the compound?

3.0 g of a mixture of potassium carbonate and potassium chloride were dissolved in a 250 cm3 standard flask. 25 cm3 of this solution required 40.00 cm3 of 0.1 M HCl for neutralization. What is the percentage by weight of K2CO3 in the mixture? (K = 39, O = 16, C = 12)

Some properties of chemical substances are mentioned below: (i) sour taste (ii) slippery to touch (iii) yields alkaline gas with ammonium salts (iv) has pH less than 7 (v) turns phenolphthalein pink. Which of the above are NOT typical properties of alkalis?
questions.explanation: A sour taste and pH below 7 are properties of acids; alkalis feel slippery, liberate NH3 from ammonium salts and turn phenolphthalein pink.

questions.stem: Hydrogen is not liberated when trioxonitrate (V) acid reacts with zinc because
options: zinc is rendered passive by the acid
hydrogen produced is oxidized to water
all nitrates are soluble in water
trioxonitrate (V) acid is a strong acid
questions.explanation: HNO3 is a strong oxidizing agent: any hydrogen formed is oxidized to water (the acid itself being reduced to oxides of nitrogen).

questions.stem: The boiling points of water, ethanol, toluene and butan-2-ol are 373.0 K, 351.3 K, 383.6 K and 372.5 K respectively. Which liquid has the highest vapour pressure at 323.0 K?
questions.explanation: The most volatile liquid (lowest boiling point, ethanol) has the highest vapour pressure at a given temperature.

questions.topic: Air as a mixture and uses of noble gases
questions.stem: In what respect will two dry samples of nitrogen gas differ from each other if sample 1 is prepared by completely removing CO2 and O2 from air and sample 2 is prepared by passing purified nitrogen (I) oxide over heated copper? Sample 1 is
options: in all respects the same as sample 2
colourless but sample 2 has a light brown colour
questions.explanation: Nitrogen from air still contains the noble gases (mainly argon, which is denser than N2), so sample 1 is slightly denser.

questions.stem: Copper sulphate solution is electrolyzed using platinum electrodes. A current of 0.193 amperes is passed for 2 hrs. How many grams of copper are deposited? (Cu = 63.5, F = 96500 coulombs)

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: What is the formula of sodium gallate if gallium (Ga) shows an oxidation number of +3?
questions.explanation: By analogy with sodium aluminate NaAl(OH)4: in NaGa(OH)4, +1 + Ga + 4(-1) = 0 gives Ga = +3.

questions.stem: If the ONLY pollutants found in the atmosphere over a city are oxides of nitrogen, suspended lead compounds, carbon monoxide and a high level of methane, the probable source(s) of the pollution must be
options: combustion of coal and automobile exhaust
combustion of coal, automobile exhaust and biological decomposition
combustion of coal and biological decomposition
questions.explanation: NOx, lead compounds and CO come from vehicle exhaust; methane from biological decomposition; coal would also give SO2, which is absent.

questions.stem: A correct electrochemical series can be obtained from K, Na, Ca, Al, Mg, Zn, Fe, Pb, H, Cu, Hg, Ag, Au by interchanging
questions.explanation: The correct order is K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Pb, H, Cu, Hg, Ag, Au: magnesium is above aluminium.

questions.stem: 2MnO4- + 10Cl- + 16H+ → 2Mn2+ + 5Cl2 + 8H2O. Which of the substances serves as an oxidizing agent?
questions.explanation: MnO4- is reduced (Mn +7 → +2), oxidizing Cl- to Cl2; so MnO4- is the oxidizing agent.

questions.stem: In the reaction H2O(g) ⇌ H2(g) + 1/2 O2(g), which of the following has no effect on the equilibrium position?
questions.explanation: An inert gas such as argon does not take part in the reaction and (at constant volume) does not change the partial pressures, so the equilibrium position is unaffected.

questions.stem: Which of the following metals will displace iron from a solution of iron (II) tetraoxosulphate (VI)?
questions.explanation: Only zinc is above iron in the electrochemical series.

questions.stem: Complete hydrogenation of ethyne yields
questions.explanation: C2H2 + 2H2 → C2H6 (ethane).

questions.stem: Which of the following is used in the manufacture of bleaching powder?
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is made by passing chlorine over slaked lime.

questions.stem: A man suspected of being drunk is made to pass his breath into acidified potassium dichromate solution. If his breath carries a significant level of ethanol, the final colour of the solution is
questions.explanation: Ethanol reduces orange dichromate(VI) to green chromium(III) ions.

questions.stem: When pollen grains are suspended in water and viewed through a microscope, they appear to be in a state of constant but erratic motion. This is due to
options: a chemical reaction between the pollen grains and water
the bombardment of the pollen grains by molecules of water
questions.explanation: Brownian motion is caused by uneven bombardment of the particles by moving water molecules.

questions.stem: The energy change (ΔH) for the reaction CO(g) + 1/2 O2(g) → CO2(g) is [ΔHf(CO) = -110.4 kJ mol-1; ΔHf(CO2) = -393 kJ mol-1]
The neutralization reaction between NaOH solution and nitrogen (IV) oxide (NO2) produces water and
questions.explanation: 2NO2 + 2NaOH → NaNO2 + NaNO3 + H2O (NO2 is a mixed acid anhydride).

questions.stem: Tetraoxosulphate (VI) ions are finally tested using
questions.explanation: SO4 2- gives a white precipitate of BaSO4 with acidified BaCl2 solution.

questions.stem: Mixing aqueous solutions of barium hydroxide and sodium tetraoxocarbonate (IV) yields a white precipitate of
questions.explanation: Ba(OH)2 + Na2CO3 → BaCO3(s) + 2NaOH; barium carbonate is insoluble.

questions.stem: An organic compound decolorized acidified KMnO4 solution but failed to react with ammoniacal silver nitrate solution. The organic compound is likely to be
questions.explanation: Unsaturation decolorizes KMnO4; failure to react with ammoniacal AgNO3 rules out a terminal alkyne, so it is an alkene.

questions.stem: Solid sodium hydroxide on exposure to air absorbs a gas and ultimately gives another alkaline substance with the molecular formula
questions.explanation: NaOH absorbs CO2 from the air: 2NaOH + CO2 → Na2CO3 + H2O.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the functional group of carboxylic acids?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl group -COOH.

questions.stem: Which of the following substances is the most abundant in the universe?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe.

questions.stem:
A colourless organic compound X was burnt in excess air to give two colourless and odourless gases, Y and Z, as products. X does not decolorize bromine vapour; Y turns lime water milky while Z gives a blue colour with anhydrous copper (II) tetraoxosulphate (VI).
Compound X is
questions.explanation: X is a saturated hydrocarbon (no reaction with bromine) burning to CO2 and H2O: an alkane.

questions.stem:
A colourless organic compound X was burnt in excess air to give two colourless and odourless gases, Y and Z, as products. X does not decolorize bromine vapour; Y turns lime water milky while Z gives a blue colour with anhydrous copper (II) tetraoxosulphate (VI).
Y and Z are respectively
questions.explanation: Y turns lime water milky (CO2); Z turns anhydrous CuSO4 blue (water).

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds is NOT the correct product formed when the parent metal is heated in air?
questions.explanation: Sodium burns in air mainly to sodium peroxide (Na2O2), not Na2O.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: The atomic number of an element whose cation, X2+, has the ground state electronic configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 is
questions.explanation: X2+ has 18 electrons, so the neutral atom has 20 electrons (calcium).

questions.stem: When marble is heated to 1473 K, another whiter solid is obtained which reacts vigorously with water to give an alkaline solution. The solution contains
questions.explanation: CaCO3 → CaO + CO2; CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2.

questions.stem: Addition of dilute hydrochloric acid to an aqueous solution of a crystalline salt yielded a yellow precipitate and a gas which turned dichromate paper green. The crystalline salt was probably
questions.explanation: Thiosulphate with dilute acid gives a yellow precipitate of sulphur and SO2, which turns acidified dichromate green.

questions.stem: The process involved in the conversion of an oil into margarine is known as
questions.explanation: Unsaturated oils are hardened into margarine by catalytic hydrogenation (Ni catalyst).

questions.stem: Which of the following roles does sodium chloride play in soap preparation? It
options: accelerates the decomposition of the fat and oil
separates the soap from the glycerol
converts the fatty acid to its sodium salt
questions.explanation: Adding NaCl 'salts out' the soap, separating it from the glycerol solution.

questions.stem: The function of sulphur during the vulcanization of rubber is to
options: act as catalyst for the polymerization of rubber molecules
convert rubber from thermosetting to thermoplastic polymer
form chains which bind rubber molecules together
shorten the chain length of rubber polymer
questions.explanation: Sulphur forms cross-links (sulphur bridges) that bind the rubber chains together, making it harder and more elastic.

questions.stem: The movement of liquid molecules from the surface of the liquid to the gaseous phase above it is known as
questions.explanation: Escape of molecules from a liquid surface into the vapour phase is evaporation.

questions.stem: 10 cm3 of hydrogen fluoride gas reacts with 5 cm3 of dinitrogen difluoride gas (N2F2) to form 10 cm3 of a single gas. Which of the following is the most likely equation for the reaction?
questions.explanation: Volumes 10:5:10 give mole ratio 2:1:2 (Gay-Lussac/Avogadro), and 2HF + N2F2 → 2NHF2 is balanced.

questions.stem: The number of chlorine atoms present in 5.85 g of NaCl is [Na = 23, Cl = 35.5; Avogadro's number = 6.02 x 10^23]
questions.explanation: 5.85/58.5 = 0.1 mol NaCl contains 0.1 × 6.02 x 10^23 = 6.02 x 10^22 chlorine atoms.

questions.stem: How much magnesium is required to react with 250 cm3 of 0.5 M HCl? [Mg = 24]
questions.explanation: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl2 + H2: HCl = 0.125 mol needs 0.0625 mol Mg = 1.5 g.

questions.stem: An element with atomic number twelve is likely to be
questions.explanation: Z = 12 (2,8,2) is magnesium, which loses two electrons to form ionic (electrovalent) compounds.

questions.stem: When 50 cm3 of a saturated solution of sugar (molar mass 342.0 g) at 40 °C was evaporated to dryness, 34.2 g of dry solid was obtained. The solubility of sugar at 40 °C is
Which of the following is an acid salt?
questions.explanation: NaHSO4 still contains replaceable hydrogen, so it is an acid salt.

questions.stem: Which of the following solutions will conduct the least amount of electricity?
options: 0.01 M aqueous solution of hexanoic acid
questions.explanation: Sugar is a non-electrolyte, producing no ions in solution.

questions.stem: In the electrolysis of an aqueous solution of K2SO4 in a cell, which species migrate to the anode?
questions.explanation: Anions move to the anode: SO4 2- and OH-.

questions.stem: How many coulombs of electricity are passed through a solution in which 6.5 amperes are allowed to run for 1.0 hour?
Which of these represents a redox reaction?
questions.explanation: Zinc is oxidized (0 → +2) and hydrogen reduced (+1 → 0); the others involve no change in oxidation numbers.

questions.stem: How many electrons are transferred in reducing one atom of Mn in the reaction MnO2 + 4HCl → MnCl2 + 2H2O + Cl2?
questions.explanation: Mn goes from +4 in MnO2 to +2 in MnCl2: two electrons gained.

questions.stem: 20 cm3 of 0.1 molar NH4OH solution when neutralized with 20.05 cm3 of 0.1 molar HCl liberated 102 joules of heat. Calculate the heat of neutralization of NH4OH.
questions.explanation: Moles neutralized = 0.002; 102 J/0.002 = 51 000 J mol-1; heat is liberated, so ΔH = -51.0 kJ mol-1.

questions.stem: The approximate volume of air containing 10 cm3 of oxygen is
questions.explanation: Air is about 21% (roughly one-fifth) oxygen, so 10 cm3 of O2 is in about 50 cm3 of air.

questions.stem: The reaction Mg + H2O → MgO + H2 takes place only in the presence of
questions.explanation: Magnesium burns in steam to give MgO and hydrogen; with hot water it gives Mg(OH)2 slowly.

questions.stem: When steam is passed through red hot carbon, which of the following are produced?
questions.explanation: C + H2O → CO + H2 (water gas).

questions.stem: Which of the following contains an efflorescent, a deliquescent and a hygroscopic substance respectively?
questions.explanation: Washing soda (Na2CO3.10H2O) effloresces, FeCl3 deliquesces, and concentrated H2SO4 is hygroscopic.

questions.stem: The exhaust fumes from a garage in a place that uses petrol of high sulphur content are bound to contain
questions.explanation: Incomplete combustion gives CO, and sulphur in the fuel burns to SO2.

questions.stem: Oxygen-demanding wastes are considered to be a water pollutant because they
options: deplete oxygen which is necessary for the survival of aquatic organisms
increase oxygen which is necessary for the survival of aquatic organisms
increase other gaseous species which are necessary for survival of aquatic organisms
deplete other gaseous species which are necessary for the survival of aquatic organisms
questions.explanation: Decomposition of such wastes uses up dissolved oxygen needed by aquatic life.

questions.stem: Which of the following will react further with oxygen to form a higher oxide?
questions.explanation: SO2 → SO3 and NO → NO2; each of the other pairs contains an oxide that is already fully oxidized.

questions.stem: In the course of an experiment, two gases X and Y were produced. X turned wet lead ethanoate paper black and Y bleached moist litmus paper. What are the element(s) in each of the gases X and Y respectively?
options: H and S; C and O
H and Cl; S and O
questions.explanation: X is H2S (blackens lead ethanoate, forming PbS) and Y is Cl2 (bleaches moist litmus).

questions.stem: Which of the following sulphides is insoluble in dilute HCl?
questions.explanation: CuS is so insoluble that it is precipitated by H2S even in acid solution; Na2S, ZnS and FeS dissolve in dilute HCl.

questions.stem: When chlorine is passed into water and subsequently exposed to sunlight, the gas evolved is
questions.explanation: Chlorine water contains HOCl, which decomposes in sunlight: 2HOCl → 2HCl + O2.

questions.stem: Which of the following metals does NOT form a stable trioxocarbonate (IV)?
questions.explanation: Aluminium carbonate is unstable and does not exist under normal conditions.

questions.stem: Ammonia gas is normally dried with
questions.explanation: Ammonia is basic, so it is dried with quicklime (CaO); H2SO4 and CaCl2 react with/absorb it.

questions.stem: What are the values of x, y and z respectively in the equation xCu + yHNO3 → xCu(NO3)2 + 4H2O + zNO?
questions.explanation: 3Cu + 8HNO3 → 3Cu(NO3)2 + 4H2O + 2NO balances all atoms.

questions.stem: The iron (III) oxide impurity in bauxite can be removed by
options: dissolution in sodium hydroxide and filtration
extraction with concentrated ammonia and reprecipitation
questions.explanation: Amphoteric Al2O3 dissolves in NaOH while basic Fe2O3 does not, so it is filtered off.

questions.stem: A white solid suspected to be lead trioxonitrate (V), zinc trioxocarbonate (IV) or calcium trioxocarbonate (IV) was heated strongly. Its residue, which was yellow when hot and white when cold, is
questions.explanation: Zinc oxide is yellow when hot and white when cold.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds would give a lilac flame coloration and a white precipitate with acidified barium chloride solution?
questions.explanation: Lilac flame indicates potassium; white precipitate with acidified BaCl2 indicates sulphate.

questions.stem: How will a metal X, which reacts explosively with air and with dilute acids, be best extracted from its ores?
options: Electrolysis of the solution of its salt
Displacement from solution by an alkali metal
questions.explanation: Very reactive metals are extracted by electrolysis of their fused (molten) salts.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT correct for the named organic compound in each case?
options: Butanoic acid solution gives effervescence with Na2CO3 solution
Glucose when reacted with Na2CrO4 at 0 °C will show immediate discharge of colour
When but-2-ene is reacted with dilute solution of KMnO4, the purple colour of KMnO4 is discharged readily even at room temperature
When butan-2-ol is boiled with butanoic acid with a drop of concentrated H2SO4, a sweet-smelling liquid is produced
questions.explanation: Glucose does not immediately decolorize chromate at 0 °C; the other statements (acid + carbonate, alkene + KMnO4, esterification) are correct.

questions.stem: Which of the following is used as an 'anti-knock' in automobile engines?
questions.explanation: Tetraethyl lead was added to petrol to reduce knocking.

questions.stem: What reaction takes place when palm-oil is added to potash and foams are observed?
questions.explanation: Alkaline hydrolysis of oil by potash forms soap (saponification).

questions.stem: How many isomers can be formed from organic compounds with the formula C3H8O?
questions.explanation: Propan-1-ol, propan-2-ol and methoxyethane: three isomers.

questions.stem: When ethanol is heated with excess concentrated sulphuric acid, the ethanol is
questions.explanation: Excess concentrated H2SO4 at about 170 °C removes water from ethanol, giving ethene.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds is NOT formed by the action of chlorine on methane?
questions.explanation: Substitution of methane gives CH3Cl, CH2Cl2, CHCl3 and CCl4; C2H5Cl has two carbons.

questions.stem: The general formula of an alkyl halide (where X represents the halide) is
questions.explanation: An alkyl group is CnH2n+1, so an alkyl halide is CnH2n+1X.

questions.stem: Which of the following are made by the process of polymerization?
questions.explanation: Nylon (condensation) and rubber (addition) are polymers.

questions.stem: Starch can be converted to ethyl alcohol by
questions.explanation: Starch is hydrolysed to sugars, which are fermented by yeast to ethanol.

questions.stem: A brand of ink containing cobalt (II), copper (II) and iron salts can best be separated into its various components by
questions.explanation: The coloured components of an ink move at different rates over an adsorbent, so chromatography separates them.

questions.stem: Which of the following substances is a mixture?
questions.explanation: Sea-water contains water with many dissolved salts in variable proportions; the others are single substances.

questions.stem: If the quantity of oxygen occupying a 2.76 litre container at a pressure of 0.825 atmosphere and 300 K is reduced by one-half, what is the pressure exerted by the remaining gas?
questions.explanation: At constant volume and temperature, pressure is proportional to the amount of gas: 0.825/2 = 0.413 atm.

questions.stem: Which of the following substances has the lowest vapour density? [O = 16, Cl = 35.5, H = 1, C = 12]
questions.explanation: Vapour density = relative molecular mass/2; ethanal (CH3CHO, 44) has the smallest molar mass (ethanoic acid 60, propanol 60, CH2Cl2 85).

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: An isotope has an atomic number of 17 and a mass number of 36. Which of the following gives the correct number of neutrons and protons (neutrons, protons) in an atom of the isotope?
questions.explanation: Protons = atomic number = 17; neutrons = 36 - 17 = 19.

questions.stem: The atomic numbers of two elements X and Y are 12 and 9 respectively. The bond in the compound formed between the atoms of these two elements is
questions.explanation: X (2,8,2) is a metal that loses 2 electrons and Y (2,7) a non-metal that gains 1, forming an ionic compound XY2.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: An element Z contains 90% of 16/8 Z and 10% of 18/8 Z. Its relative atomic mass is
questions.explanation: Relative atomic mass = 0.9 × 16 + 0.1 × 18 = 16.2.

questions.stem: The greater the difference in electronegativity between bonded atoms, the
options: lower the polarity of the bond
higher the polarity of the bond
higher the possibility of the substance formed being a molecule
questions.explanation: A larger electronegativity difference gives a more polar (more ionic) bond.

questions.stem: A stream of air was successively passed through three tubes X, Y and Z containing a concentrated aqueous solution of KOH, red hot copper powder and fused calcium chloride respectively. What was the composition of the gas emanating from tube Z?
options: N2, CO2 and the inert gases
Water vapour, N2 and the inert gases
questions.explanation: KOH absorbs CO2, hot copper removes O2 and fused CaCl2 removes water vapour, leaving nitrogen and the noble gases.

questions.stem: In the purification of town water supply, alum is used principally to
options: improve the taste of the water
questions.explanation: Alum causes fine suspended particles to coagulate and settle.

questions.stem: Which of the following water samples will have the highest titre value when titrated for the Ca2+ ions using soap solution?
options: Rain water stored in a glass jar for two years
Permanently hard water passed through permutit
questions.explanation: Boiling does not remove permanent hardness, so that sample still contains Ca2+ and needs the most soap; the others have been softened.

questions.stem: Oil spillage in ponds and creeks can be cleaned up by
questions.explanation: Detergents emulsify and disperse the oil.

questions.stem: The solubility of Na3AsO4.12H2O is 38.9 g per 100 g H2O. What is the percentage of Na3AsO4 in the saturated solution? [As = 75, Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: M(hydrate) = 424, M(Na3AsO4) = 208; anhydrous salt = 38.9 × 208/424 = 19.1 g in 138.9 g of solution = 13.7%. (The paper printed O = 12; O = 16 is needed.)

questions.stem: Which is the correct set of results for tests conducted respectively on fresh lime juice and ethanol?
options: Add crystals of NaHCO3: lime juice - gas evolved; ethanol - no gas evolved
Test with methyl orange: lime juice - turns colourless; ethanol - no change
Taste: lime juice - bitter; ethanol - sour
Add a piece of sodium: lime juice - no gas evolved; ethanol - H2 evolved
questions.explanation: Lime juice is acidic (citric acid) and liberates CO2 from NaHCO3, whereas neutral ethanol does not.

questions.stem: In which of the following are the aqueous solutions of each of the substances correctly arranged in order of decreasing acidity?
options: Ethanoic acid, milk of magnesia, sodium chloride, hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide
Ethanoic acid, hydrochloric acid, milk of magnesia, sodium chloride and sodium hydroxide
Hydrochloric acid, ethanoic acid, sodium chloride, milk of magnesia and sodium hydroxide
Hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, sodium chloride, ethanoic acid and milk of magnesia
questions.explanation: Strong acid HCl > weak acid ethanoic acid > neutral NaCl > weak base milk of magnesia > strong base NaOH.

questions.stem: The basicity of tetraoxophosphate (V) acid is
questions.explanation: H3PO4 has three replaceable hydrogen ions, so its basicity is 3.

questions.stem: If 24.83 cm3 of 0.15 M NaOH is titrated to its end point with 39.45 cm3 of HCl, what is the molarity of the HCl?
questions.explanation: NaOH and HCl react 1:1, so M = 24.83 x 0.15/39.45 = 0.094 M.

questions.stem: A quantity of electricity liberates 3.6 g of silver from its salt. What mass of aluminium will be liberated from its salt by the same quantity of electricity?
Which of the following statements is CORRECT if 1 Faraday of electricity is passed through 1 M CuSO4 solution for 1 minute?
options: The pH of the solution at the cathode decreases
The pH of the solution at the anode decreases
1 mole of Cu will be liberated at the cathode
60 moles of Cu will be liberated at the anode
questions.explanation: OH- ions are discharged at the anode, leaving excess H+ there, so the pH at the anode falls; 1 F deposits only 0.5 mol Cu at the cathode.

questions.stem: What mass of magnesium would be obtained by passing a current of 2 amperes for 2 hrs 30 mins through molten magnesium chloride? [1 faraday = 96500 coulombs, Mg = 24]
questions.explanation: Q = 2 x 9000 = 18000 C; Mg2+ needs 2 F per mole, so mass = 18000/(2 x 96500) x 24 = 2.24 g.

questions.stem: In the reaction 3CuO + 2NH3 -> 3Cu + 3H2O + N2, how many electrons are transferred for each mole of copper produced?
questions.explanation: Each Cu2+ gains 2 electrons, so 1 mol Cu needs 2 x 6.02 x 10^23 = 1.2 x 10^24 electrons.

questions.stem: Z is a solid substance which liberates carbon (IV) oxide on treatment with concentrated H2SO4 and KMnO4. The solid substance Z is
questions.explanation: Ethanedioic acid is a solid reducing agent that is oxidised by KMnO4 (and dehydrated by conc. H2SO4) to give carbon (IV) oxide.

questions.stem: 5 g of ammonium trioxonitrate (V) on dissolution in water cooled its surrounding water and container by 1.6 kJ. What is the heat of solution of NH4NO3? [N = 14, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: 5 g = 5/80 = 0.0625 mol absorbs 1.6 kJ, so the heat of solution = +1.6/0.0625 = +25.6 kJ/mol (endothermic).

questions.stem: Tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid is prepared using the chemical reaction SO3(g) + H2O(l) -> H2SO4(l). Given the heats of formation for SO3(g), H2O(l) and H2SO4(l) as -395 kJ mol^-1, -286 kJ mol^-1 and -811 kJ mol^-1 respectively, the heat of reaction is
questions.explanation: Heat of reaction = -811 - (-395 + -286) = -130 kJ.

questions.stem: The times taken for iodine to be liberated in the reaction between sodium thiosulphate and hydrochloric acid at various temperatures are as follows: Temperature (°C): 25, 35, 45; Time (seconds): 72, 36, 18. These results suggest that
options: for a 10° rise in temperature, rate of reaction is doubled
for a 10° rise in temperature, rate of reaction is halved
time taken for iodine to appear does not depend on temperature
for a 10° rise in temperature, rate of reaction is tripled
questions.explanation: The time halves for every 10° rise (72 -> 36 -> 18 s), so the rate doubles.

questions.stem: The reaction between sulphur (IV) oxide and oxygen is represented by the equilibrium reaction 2SO2(g) + O2(g) <=> 2SO3(g), ΔH = -196 kJ. What factor would influence increased production of SO3(g)?
options: Increase in the temperature of the reaction
Decrease in the temperature of SO2(g)
Decrease in the concentration of SO2(g)
questions.explanation: The forward reaction is exothermic, so lowering the temperature shifts the equilibrium to the right; a catalyst does not change the equilibrium yield.

questions.stem: Which of the following equations correctly represents the action of hot concentrated alkaline solution on chlorine?
questions.explanation: Hot concentrated alkali disproportionates chlorine into chlorate (V) and chloride ions in solution in a 1:5 ratio; option A is the reaction with cold dilute alkali.

questions.stem: Magnesium ribbon was allowed to burn inside a given gas P leaving a white solid residue Q. Addition of water to Q liberated a gas which produced dense white fumes with a drop of hydrochloric acid. The gas P was
questions.explanation: Magnesium burns in nitrogen to form Mg3N2, which reacts with water to give ammonia; ammonia forms white fumes of NH4Cl with HCl.

questions.stem: In which of the following pairs of elements is allotropy exhibited by each element?
questions.explanation: Oxygen (O2 and O3) and sulphur (rhombic, monoclinic, etc.) both show allotropy.

questions.stem: Which of the following gases can best be used for demonstrating the fountain experiment? (i) Nitrogen (ii) Ammonia (iii) Nitrogen (I) oxide (iv) Hydrogen chloride
questions.explanation: The fountain experiment needs a very soluble gas; ammonia and hydrogen chloride are both extremely soluble in water.

questions.stem: When calcium hydroxide is heated with ammonium tetraoxosulphate (VI), the gas given off may be collected by
options: bubbling it through water and then passing it through calcium oxide
passing it directly through calcium oxide
passing it directly through calcium chloride
questions.explanation: The gas is ammonia, which is dried with calcium oxide; it reacts with conc. H2SO4 and with CaCl2, and dissolves in water.

questions.stem: Stainless steel is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Stainless steel is iron with carbon and chromium (often nickel), and the chromium resists corrosion.

questions.stem: Alloys are best prepared by
options: high temperature arc welding of the metals
electrolysis using the major metallic component as cathode
reducing a mixture of the oxides of the elements
cooling a molten mixture of the necessary elements
questions.explanation: Alloys are made by melting the components together and allowing the molten mixture to cool and solidify.

questions.stem: In spite of the electronic configuration 1s^2 2s^2 2p^2, carbon is tetravalent because
options: the electrons in both 2s and 2p orbitals have equal energy
the electrons in both 2s and 2p orbitals are equivalent
the six orbitals hybridize to four
questions.explanation: One 2s electron is promoted and the 2s and three 2p orbitals hybridize (sp3), giving four equivalent half-filled orbitals.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds will give a precipitate with an aqueous ammoniacal solution of copper (I) chloride?
questions.explanation: Only terminal alkynes (with an acidic ≡C-H) form a red copper (I) acetylide precipitate; but-1-yne is terminal.

questions.stem: The efficiency of petrol as a fuel in high compression internal combustion engines improves with an increase in the amount of
questions.explanation: Branched-chain alkanes resist knocking (higher octane number), improving performance in high-compression engines.

questions.stem: Ethanol reacts with aqueous sodium mono-oxoiodate (I) to give a bright yellow solid with a characteristic smell. The product is
questions.explanation: This is the iodoform test: ethanol gives yellow triiodomethane (CHI3) crystals.

questions.stem: The most volatile fraction obtained from fractional distillation of crude petroleum contains
questions.explanation: The refinery gas fraction, which has the lowest boiling point, is made up of the C1-C4 alkanes such as methane, ethane and propane.

questions.stem: Local black soap is made by boiling palm oil with liquid extract of ash. The function of the ash is to provide the
questions.explanation: Wood ash extract contains alkali (potassium carbonate/hydroxide), which saponifies the oil.

questions.stem: Synthetic rubber is made by polymerization of
questions.explanation: Rubber is poly(2-methylbuta-1,3-diene), that is, polymerized isoprene.

questions.stem: Complete oxidation of propan-1-ol gives
questions.explanation: A primary alkanol is oxidised first to the alkanal and then completely to the alkanoic acid: propanoic acid.

questions.stem: In the experiment above (solid ammonium chloride heated at the bottom of a tilted tube), ammonium chloride crystals deposit on the walls of the tube as a result of
questions.explanation: Ammonium chloride sublimes: it changes directly to vapour on heating and back to solid on the cooler part of the tube.

questions.stem: The formula of the compound formed in a reaction between a trivalent metal M and a tetravalent non-metal X is
questions.explanation: Exchange the valencies: M (3) and X (4) give M4X3.

questions.stem: 2.25 g of a sample of an oxide of copper on reduction gave 2.0 g of copper. 2.50 g of another oxide of copper on reduction also gave 2.0 g of copper. These results are in accordance with the law of
questions.explanation: For a fixed 2.0 g of copper the oxygen masses are 0.25 g and 0.50 g, a simple ratio of 1:2, which is the law of multiple proportions.

questions.stem: One mole of propane is mixed with five moles of oxygen. The mixture is ignited and the propane burns completely. What is the volume of the products at s.t.p? [G.M.V = 22.4 dm^3 mol^-1]
questions.explanation: C3H8 + 5O2 -> 3CO2 + 4H2O; at s.t.p. the water is liquid, so only 3 mol CO2 remain as gas: 3 x 22.4 = 67.2 dm^3.

questions.stem: A graph of the volume of a fixed mass of gas (vertical axis) against temperature in kelvin (horizontal axis) is a straight line passing through the origin. Which of the gas laws does the graph illustrate?
questions.explanation: V proportional to T (in kelvin) at constant pressure is Charles' law.

questions.stem: The forces holding naphthalene crystal together can be overcome when naphthalene is heated to a temperature of 354 K resulting in the crystals melting. These forces are known as
questions.explanation: Naphthalene is a molecular solid whose molecules are held by weak van der Waals forces, hence its low melting point.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: A metallic ion X^2+ with an inert gas structure contains 18 electrons. How many protons are there in this ion?
questions.explanation: X lost 2 electrons to form X^2+, so the neutral atom had 20 electrons and therefore 20 protons.

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: Which of the following physical properties decreases across the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Across a period the nuclear charge increases and pulls the electrons closer, so atomic radius decreases while the others generally increase.

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: What are the possible oxidation numbers for an element if its atomic number is 17?
questions.explanation: Element 17 (chlorine, 2,8,7) can gain one electron (-1) or use all seven valence electrons (+7).

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: The energy change accompanying the addition of an electron to a gaseous atom is called
questions.explanation: Electron affinity is the energy change when a gaseous atom gains an electron.

questions.stem: 1.34 g of hydrated sodium tetraoxosulphate (VI) was heated to give an anhydrous salt weighing 0.71 g. The formula of the hydrated salt is [Na = 23, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: Na2SO4 = 0.71/142 = 0.005 mol; water = 0.63/18 = 0.035 mol; the ratio 1:7 gives Na2SO4.7H2O.

questions.stem: The ion that may be assumed to have negligible concentration in a sample of water that lathers readily with soap is
questions.explanation: Hardness (poor lathering) is caused by Ca^2+ and Mg^2+; water that lathers readily has negligible Mg^2+.

questions.stem: Which of the following dilute solutions has the lowest pH value?
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid is a strong, fully ionised acid, so it has the highest H+ concentration and lowest pH.

questions.stem: Which of the following in aqueous solution is neutral to litmus?
questions.explanation: NaCl is the salt of a strong acid and a strong base and does not hydrolyse; NH4Cl and FeCl3 are acidic and Na2CO3 is alkaline.

questions.stem: What volume of a 0.1 M H3PO4 will be required to neutralize 45.0 cm^3 of a 0.2 M NaOH?
questions.explanation: H3PO4 + 3NaOH: mol NaOH = 0.009, so mol H3PO4 = 0.003 and volume = 0.003/0.1 = 0.030 dm^3 = 30.0 cm^3.

questions.stem: Which of the following substances is a basic salt?
questions.explanation: A basic salt contains replaceable hydroxide; Mg(OH)Cl is a basic salt (NaHCO3 is an acid salt, alum a double salt).

questions.stem: Which of the following acts both as a reducing and an oxidizing agent?
questions.explanation: Sulphur in SO2 (+4) can be oxidised to +6 or reduced (e.g. by H2S to S), so SO2 acts as both.

questions.stem: Which of the following reactions takes place in the cathode compartment during the electrolysis of copper (II) chloride solution?
questions.explanation: Reduction occurs at the cathode: copper (II) ions gain electrons and are deposited as copper.

questions.stem: A mixture of starch solution and potassium iodide was placed in a test tube. On adding dilute tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid and then K2Cr2O7 solution, a blue-black colour was produced. In this reaction, the
options: tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid acts as an oxidizing agent
questions.explanation: Acidified dichromate oxidises I^- to I2, which gives the blue-black colour with starch; the dichromate is reduced.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the dissolution of sodium hydroxide in water is TRUE?
options: The dissolution of NaOH(s) in water is endothermic
The heat of solution of NaOH(s) is positive
The NaOH(s) gains heat from the surroundings
The heat of solution of NaOH(s) is negative
questions.explanation: Dissolving NaOH releases heat (the solution warms), so the process is exothermic and the heat of solution is negative.

questions.stem: Which of the following will produce the greatest increase in the rate of the chemical reaction represented by the equation Na2S2O3(aq) + 2HCl(aq) -> 2NaCl(aq) + H2O(l) + SO2(g) + S(s)?
options: A decrease in temperature and an increase in the concentration of the reactants
An increase in the temperature and a decrease in the concentration of the reactants
An increase in the temperature and an increase in the concentrations of the reactants
A decrease in the temperature and a decrease in the concentration of the reactants
questions.explanation: Raising both temperature and concentration increases the frequency and energy of collisions, giving the largest rate increase.

questions.stem: Which property of a reversible reaction is affected by a catalyst?
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative pathway of lower activation energy; it does not change ΔH, ΔG or the equilibrium position.

questions.stem: Which of the following is used in fire extinguishers?
questions.explanation: CO2 is dense, does not burn and does not support combustion, so it smothers fires.

questions.stem: When H2S gas is passed into a solution of iron (III) chloride, the colour changes from yellow to green. This is because
options: Fe^3+ ions are oxidized by H2S
Fe^3+ ions are reduced to Fe^3+ ions
questions.explanation: Fe^3+ (yellow) oxidises H2S to sulphur and is itself reduced to green Fe^2+.

questions.stem: In the reaction C6H10O5(s) -> 6C(s) + 5H2O, concentrated H2SO4 is acting as
questions.explanation: Concentrated H2SO4 removes the elements of water from the carbohydrate, leaving carbon, so it is acting as a dehydrating agent.

questions.stem: Suitable reagents for the laboratory preparation of nitrogen are
questions.explanation: Warming NaNO2 with NH4Cl forms ammonium nitrite, which decomposes to nitrogen and water.

questions.stem: Chlorine is produced commercially by
questions.explanation: Industrial chlorine comes from the electrolysis of brine (concentrated NaCl solution).

questions.stem: Which of the following is used in the manufacture of glass?
questions.explanation: Glass is made by fusing sand with sodium carbonate (soda ash) and limestone.

questions.stem: Aluminium is extracted commercially from its ore by
options: heating aluminium oxide with coke in a furnace
the electrolysis of fused aluminium oxide in cryolite
treating cryolite with sodium hydroxide solution under pressure
heating sodium aluminium silicate to a high temperature
questions.explanation: Aluminium is too reactive to be reduced by carbon, so purified alumina dissolved in molten cryolite is electrolysed.

questions.stem: Crude copper can be purified by the electrolysis of CuSO4(aq) if
options: the crude copper is made the anode of the cell
the crude copper is made the cathode of the cell
questions.explanation: The impure copper anode dissolves and pure copper is deposited on a pure copper cathode.

questions.stem: Alkanoates are formed by the reaction of alkanoic acids with
questions.explanation: Esterification: alkanoic acid + alkanol -> alkanoate (ester) + water.

questions.stem: The four classes of hydrocarbons are
questions.explanation: The hydrocarbon classes are alkanes, alkenes, alkynes and aromatic hydrocarbons; the other options list individual compounds.

questions.stem: Alkanes -> (400-700 °C, catalyst) smaller alkanes + alkenes + hydrogen. The above reaction is known as
questions.explanation: Breaking large alkanes into smaller alkanes, alkenes and hydrogen using heat and a catalyst is cracking.

questions.stem: In the reaction 2(C6H10O5)n + nH2O -> nC12H22O11 (diastase), diastase is functioning as
questions.explanation: Diastase is an enzyme, a biological catalyst, that hydrolyses starch to maltose.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: Butan-1-ol molecules form hydrogen bonds, giving it the highest boiling point among these compounds of similar size.

questions.stem: Detergents have the general formula
questions.explanation: Soapless detergents are sodium alkyl (benzene) sulphonates, RSO3^-Na^+; RCO2^-Na^+ is the formula of a soap.

questions.stem: What process would coal undergo to give coal gas, coal tar, ammoniacal liquor and coke?
questions.explanation: Heating coal strongly in the absence of air (destructive distillation) yields coal gas, coal tar, ammoniacal liquor and coke.

questions.stem: Which of the following would support the conclusion that a solid sample is a mixture?
options: The solid can be ground to a fine powder
The density of the solid is 2.25 g dm^-3
The solid has a melting range of 300 °C to 375 °C
The solid absorbs moisture from the atmosphere
questions.explanation: A pure substance melts sharply at a fixed temperature; melting over a wide range shows the sample is impure (a mixture).

questions.stem: The molar ratio of carbon to hydrogen of a volatile liquid compound is 1:2. 0.12 g of the liquid on evaporation at s.t.p gave 32 cm^3 of vapour. The molecular formula of the liquid is [G.M.V = 22.4 dm^3, C = 12, H = 1]
questions.explanation: Molar mass = 0.12 x 22400/32 = 84; (CH2)n = 14n = 84 gives n = 6, so C6H12.

questions.stem: 20.00 cm^3 of a solution containing 0.53 g of anhydrous Na2CO3 in 100 cm^3 requires 25.00 cm^3 of H2SO4 for complete neutralization. The concentration of the acid solution in moles per dm^3 is [H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Na = 23, S = 32]
The minimum volume of oxygen required for the complete combustion of a mixture of 10 cm^3 of CO and 15 cm^3 of H2 is
questions.explanation: 2CO + O2 and 2H2 + O2 each need half their volume of oxygen: 5 + 7.5 = 12.5 cm^3.

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: The atomic radii of Li, Na and K are 1.33 Å, 1.54 Å and 1.96 Å respectively. Which of the following explains this gradation in atomic radius?
options: Electropositivity decreases from Li to Na to K
Electronegativity decreases from Li to Na to K
The number of electron shells increases from Li to Na to K
The elements are in the same period
questions.explanation: Down a group each element has an extra electron shell, so atomic radius increases.

questions.stem: Elements X and Y have electronic configurations 1s^2 2s^2 2p^4 and 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^1 respectively. When they combine, the formula of the compound formed is
questions.explanation: X (oxygen) has valency 2 and Y (aluminium) valency 3, so the compound is Y2X3.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: The atomic number of caesium is 55 and its atomic mass is 133. The nucleus of the caesium atom therefore contains
questions.explanation: Protons = 55; neutrons = 133 - 55 = 78 (electrons are not in the nucleus).

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: Four elements P, Q, R and S have atomic numbers of 4, 10, 12 and 14 respectively. Which of these elements is a noble gas?
questions.explanation: Atomic number 10 (2,8) is neon, which has a complete octet.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: How many valence electrons are contained in the element represented by 31P (atomic number 15)?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus is 2,8,5, so it has 5 valence electrons.

questions.stem: The gaseous pollutant sulphur (IV) oxide is most likely to be detected in fairly reasonable quantities in the area around a plant for the
questions.explanation: Copper is smelted from sulphide ores; roasting them releases SO2.

questions.stem: A hydrated salt of formula MSO4.XH2O contains 45.3% by mass of the water of crystallization. Calculate the value of X. [M = 56, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1]

Using 50 cm^3 of 1 M potassium hydroxide and 100 cm^3 of 1 M tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid, calculate the respective volumes in cm^3 of base and acid that would be required to produce the maximum amount of potassium tetraoxosulphate (VI). [K = 39, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: 2KOH + H2SO4 -> K2SO4 + 2H2O: all 50 cm^3 (0.05 mol) of KOH reacts with 0.025 mol acid = 25 cm^3.

questions.stem: A solution of calcium bromide contains 20 g dm^-3. What is the molarity of the solution with respect to calcium bromide and bromide ions? [Ca = 40, Br = 80]
questions.explanation: CaBr2 = 200 g/mol, so 20 g/dm^3 = 0.1 M; each formula unit gives 2 Br^-, so [Br^-] = 0.2 M.

questions.stem: An acid and its conjugate base
options: can neutralize each other to form a salt
differ only by the opposite charges they carry
questions.explanation: By the Bronsted-Lowry definition, a conjugate acid-base pair differs by one proton (H+).

questions.stem: The same current is passed for the same time through solutions of AgNO3 and CuSO4 connected in series. How much silver will be deposited if 1.0 g of copper is produced? [Cu = 63.5, S = 32, O = 16, Ag = 108, N = 14]
questions.explanation: 1.0 g Cu = 1/63.5 mol needing 2/63.5 F; that deposits 2/63.5 x 108 = 3.4 g Ag.

questions.stem: What is discharged at the cathode during the electrolysis of copper (II) tetraoxosulphate (VI) solution?
questions.explanation: Cu^2+ is lower than H+ in the electrochemical series, so it is preferentially discharged at the cathode.

questions.stem: An element Z forms an anion whose formula is [Z(CN)6]^y. If Z has an oxidation number of +2, what is the value of y?
Which of the reactions is NOT an example of a redox reaction? I. Fe + 2Ag^+ -> Fe^2+ + 2Ag  II. 2H2S + SO2 -> 2H2O + 3S  III. N2 + O2 -> 2NO  IV. CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2
questions.explanation: Only the decomposition of CaCO3 involves no change in oxidation numbers; I, II and III all involve electron transfer.

questions.stem: The combustion of ethene, C2H4, is given by the equation C2H4 + 3O2 -> 2CO2 + 2H2O; ΔH = -1428 kJ. If the molar heats of formation of water and carbon (IV) oxide are -286 kJ and -396 kJ respectively, calculate the molar heat of formation of ethene in kJ.

CO(g) + H2O(g) <=> CO2(g) + H2(g); ΔH = -41000 J. Which of the following factors favour the formation of hydrogen in the above reaction? I. high pressure II. low pressure III. high temperature IV. use of excess steam
questions.explanation: Moles of gas are equal on both sides, so pressure has no effect; the forward reaction is exothermic, so high temperature is unfavourable; excess steam shifts the equilibrium to the right.

questions.stem: Which of the following represents the balanced equation for the reaction of copper with concentrated trioxonitrate (V) acid?
questions.explanation: Concentrated HNO3 is reduced to brown NO2; the equation with 8HNO3 producing NO is for dilute acid.

questions.stem: The catalyst used in the contact process for the manufacture of tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid is
questions.explanation: SO2 is oxidised to SO3 over vanadium (V) oxide in the contact process.

questions.stem: Some products of destructive distillation of coal are
questions.explanation: Destructive distillation of coal gives coke, coal tar, ammoniacal liquor and coal gas.

questions.stem: Gunpowder is made from charcoal, sulphur and potassium trioxonitrate (V). The salt in the mixture performs the function of
questions.explanation: KNO3 supplies oxygen for the rapid combustion of the charcoal and sulphur, so it is the oxidant.

questions.stem: Which of the following reactions is (are) feasible? I. Br2(l) + 2Cl^-(aq) -> 2Br^-(aq) + Cl2(aq)  II. 2I^-(aq) + Br2(l) -> 2Br^-(aq) + I2(s)  III. 2F^-(aq) + Cl2(aq) -> 2Cl^-(aq) + F2(g)  IV. 2F^-(aq) + Br2(l) -> 2Br^-(aq) + F2(g)
questions.explanation: A halogen can only displace a less reactive (lower) halogen from its salts; bromine displaces iodide but not chloride or fluoride.

questions.stem: Bleaching powder, CaOCl2.H2O, deteriorates on exposure to air because
options: it loses its water of crystallization
atmospheric nitrogen displaces chlorine from it
carbon (IV) oxide of the atmosphere displaces chlorine from it
bleaching agents should be stored in solution
questions.explanation: Atmospheric CO2 reacts with bleaching powder, liberating chlorine, so it loses its bleaching power.

questions.stem: The products of the thermal decomposition of ammonium trioxonitrate (V) are
questions.explanation: NH4NO3 -> N2O + 2H2O on gentle heating.

questions.stem: Mortar is NOT used for under-water construction because
options: it hardens by loss of water
its hardening does not depend upon evaporation
it will be washed away by the flow of water
questions.explanation: Mortar sets as it loses water (and absorbs CO2 from air), which cannot happen under water.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT involved in the extraction of metals from their ores?
questions.explanation: Metals occur as positive ions in ores and are extracted by reduction, not oxidation.

questions.stem: When excess chlorine is mixed with ethene at room temperature, the product is
questions.explanation: Chlorine adds across the C=C double bond, giving CH2Cl-CH2Cl (1,2-dichloroethane).

questions.stem: Vulcanization of rubber is a process by which
options: isoprene units are joined to produce rubber
sulphur is chemically combined in the rubber
water is removed from the rubber
questions.explanation: Vulcanization heats rubber with sulphur, forming sulphur cross-links that make it harder and more elastic.

questions.stem: The reaction between ethanoic acid and sodium hydroxide is an example of
questions.explanation: An acid reacting with a base to give a salt (sodium ethanoate) and water is neutralization.

questions.stem: The bond which joins two ethanoic acid molecules in the liquid state is
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid molecules associate as dimers held together by hydrogen bonds between -COOH groups.

questions.stem: The alkaline hydrolysis of fats and oils produces soap and
questions.explanation: Saponification of a triglyceride gives soap and glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol).

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name for the compound CH2=C(CH3)-CH2Cl?
questions.explanation: Number from the end nearest the double bond: the C=C is at C1, the methyl at C2 and the chlorine at C3, giving 3-chloro-2-methylprop-1-ene.

questions.stem: The gas responsible for most of the fatal explosions in coal mines is
questions.explanation: Methane (firedamp) forms explosive mixtures with air in coal mines.

questions.stem: Three liquids X, Y and Z containing only hydrogen and carbon were burnt on a spoon. X and Y burnt with sooty flames while Z did not. Y is able to discharge the colour of bromine water whereas X and Z cannot. Which of the liquids would be aromatic in nature?
questions.explanation: A sooty flame shows a high carbon content; X is not unsaturated in the alkene sense (it does not decolourise bromine water), so X is aromatic.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a physical change?
options: The bubbling of chlorine into water
The bubbling of chlorine into a jar containing hydrogen
The dissolution of sodium chloride in water
The passing of steam over heated iron
questions.explanation: Dissolving salt forms no new substance and the salt is recovered by evaporation; chlorine reacts with water and with hydrogen, and steam oxidises iron.

questions.stem: Changes in the physical states of a chemical substance T are shown in the scheme: Solid T -> Gaseous T (X); Gaseous T -> Liquid T (Y); Liquid T -> Solid T (Z). The letters X, Y and Z respectively represent
questions.explanation: Solid to gas is sublimation, gas to liquid is condensation and liquid to solid is freezing.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: The Avogadro's number of 24 g of magnesium is the same as that of
questions.explanation: 24 g Mg is 1 mol (6.02 x 10^23 atoms); 32 g of O2 is also 1 mol of molecules, while the others are 0.5 mol.

questions.stem: If a gas occupies a container of volume 146 cm^3 at 18 °C and 0.971 atm, its volume in cm^3 at s.t.p is
The volume occupied by 1.58 g of a gas at s.t.p is 500 cm^3. What is the relative molecular mass of the gas? [G.M.V at s.t.p = 22.40 dm^3]
A basic postulate of the kinetic theory of gases is that the molecules of a gas move in straight lines between collisions. This implies that
options: forces of repulsion and attraction are in equilibrium
questions.explanation: Straight-line motion means no net force acts on a molecule between collisions, so any attractive and repulsive forces cancel out.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: Atoms P, Q, R and S have the following particles: P - 13 protons, 13 electrons, 14 neutrons; Q - 16 protons, 16 electrons, 16 neutrons; R - 17 protons, 17 electrons, 35 neutrons; S - 19 protons, 19 electrons, 20 neutrons. Which of the four atoms can be described by the following properties: relative atomic mass is greater than 30 but less than 40; it has an odd atomic number and forms a unipositive ion in solution?
questions.explanation: S has mass 19 + 20 = 39 and an odd atomic number of 19 (potassium), and it forms K+; P has mass 27, Q has an even atomic number and R has mass 52.

questions.stem: Which of the following terms indicates the number of bonds that can be formed by an atom?
questions.explanation: Valence (valency) is the combining power of an atom, that is, the number of bonds it can form.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: Chlorine, consisting of two isotopes of mass numbers 35 and 37, has an atomic mass of 35.5. The relative abundance of the isotope of mass number 37 is

10.0 dm^3 of air containing H2S as an impurity was passed through a solution of Pb(NO3)2 until all the H2S had reacted. The precipitate of PbS was found to weigh 5.02 g. According to the equation Pb(NO3)2 + H2S -> PbS + 2HNO3, the percentage by volume of hydrogen sulphide in the air is [Pb = 207, S = 32, GMV at s.t.p = 22.4 dm^3]
questions.explanation: PbS = 5.02/239 = 0.0210 mol, so the H2S volume = 0.0210 x 22.4 = 0.470 dm^3, which is 4.70% of 10.0 dm^3. (The paper misprints S = 23.)

questions.stem: A blue solid, T, which weighed 5.0 g was placed on a table. After 8 hours, the resulting pink solid was found to weigh 5.5 g. It can be inferred that substance T
options: has some molecules of water of crystallization
questions.explanation: T absorbed moisture from the air and gained mass but stayed solid (it did not dissolve), so it is hygroscopic.

questions.stem: The effluent of an industrial plant used in the electrolysis of concentrated brine with a flowing mercury cathode may contain impurities like
questions.explanation: Mercury-cathode cells can release mercury compounds such as mercury (II) chloride in their effluent, a serious pollutant.

questions.stem: The solubility in moles per dm^3 of 20 g of CuSO4 dissolved in 100 g of water at 18 °C is [Cu = 63.5, S = 32, O = 16]
questions.explanation: 20 g = 20/159.5 = 0.125 mol per 100 g water, which is 1.25 mol per 1000 g (about 1 dm^3) of water.

questions.stem: Smoke consists of
options: solid or liquid particles dispersed in gas
gas or liquid particles dispersed in liquid
questions.explanation: Smoke is an aerosol of tiny solid (or liquid) particles dispersed in a gas (air).
