questions.stem: Na2C2O4 + CaCl2 -> CaC2O4 + 2NaCl. Given a solution of 1.9 g of sodium oxalate in 50 g of water at room temperature, calculate the minimum volume of 0.1 M calcium chloride required to produce maximum calcium oxalate using the above equation.

2.0 g of a monobasic acid was made up to 250 cm^3 with distilled water. 25.00 cm^3 of this solution required 20.00 cm^3 of 0.1 M NaOH solution for complete neutralization. The molar mass of the acid is
questions.explanation: Moles of NaOH = 0.002, so there are 0.002 mol of acid in 25 cm^3 and 0.02 mol in 250 cm^3; molar mass = 2.0/0.02 = 100 g.

questions.stem: What is the concentration of H+ ions in moles per dm^3 of a solution of pH 4.398?
If 10.8 g of silver is deposited in a silver coulometer connected in series with a copper coulometer, the volume of oxygen liberated is [Ag = 108, Cu = 64, GMV at s.t.p = 22.40 dm^3]
questions.explanation: 10.8 g Ag = 0.1 F; O2 needs 4 F per mole, so 0.1/4 x 22.4 = 0.56 dm^3.

questions.stem: 0.1 faraday of electricity deposited 2.95 g of nickel during electrolysis of an aqueous solution. Calculate the number of moles of nickel that will be deposited by 0.4 faraday. [Ni = 58.7]
questions.explanation: 0.1 F deposits 2.95/58.7 = 0.050 mol, so 0.4 F deposits 4 x 0.050 = 0.20 mol.

questions.stem: Cr2O7^2- + 6Fe^2+ + 14H^+ -> 2Cr^3+ + 6Fe^3+ + 7H2O. In the above reaction, chromium changes from
questions.explanation: In Cr2O7^2-, 2x + 7(-2) = -2 gives x = +6; it is reduced to Cr^3+ (+3).

questions.stem: In the reaction IO3^- + 5I^- + 6H^+ -> 3I2 + 3H2O, the oxidizing agent is
questions.explanation: Iodine in IO3^- goes from +5 to 0 (it is reduced), so IO3^- is the oxidizing agent.

questions.stem: Iron galvanized with zinc is cathodically protected from corrosion. This is because
options: zinc has a more positive oxidation potential than iron
zinc has a less positive oxidation potential than iron
both have the same oxidation potential
questions.explanation: Zinc is more readily oxidised than iron, so it corrodes sacrificially and the iron acts as the cathode.

questions.stem: Which of the following samples will react fastest with dilute trioxonitrate (V) acid?
options: 5 g of lumps of CaCO3 at 25 °C
5 g of lumps of CaCO3 at 50 °C
questions.explanation: Larger surface area (powder) and higher temperature both increase the reaction rate.

questions.stem: In the reaction 2HI(g) <=> H2(g) + I2(g), ΔH = +10 kJ, the concentration of iodine in the equilibrium mixture can be increased by
questions.explanation: The forward reaction is endothermic, so raising the temperature shifts the equilibrium to the right; pressure has no effect because moles of gas are equal on both sides.

questions.stem: Which of the following gases can be collected by upward displacement of air?
questions.explanation: Upward displacement of air (downward delivery) is used for gases denser than air; chlorine is much denser than air.

questions.stem: In the Haber process for the manufacture of ammonia, the catalyst commonly used is finely divided
questions.explanation: The Haber process uses finely divided iron (with promoters) as the catalyst.

questions.stem: Which of the following metals will liberate hydrogen from steam or dilute acid?
questions.explanation: Iron is above hydrogen in the activity series and reacts with steam (giving Fe3O4 + H2) and with dilute acids.

questions.stem: Coal fire should not be used in poorly ventilated rooms because
options: of the accumulation of CO2 which causes deep sleep
of the accumulation of CO which causes suffocation
it removes most of the gases in the room
questions.explanation: Incomplete combustion in limited air produces poisonous carbon (II) oxide, which combines with haemoglobin and causes suffocation.

questions.stem: The major component of the slag from the production of iron is
options: an alloy of calcium and iron
questions.explanation: Limestone decomposes to CaO, which combines with silica impurities to form slag, CaSiO3.

questions.stem: Sodium hydroxide should be stored in properly closed containers because it
options: readily absorbs water vapour from the air
is easily oxidized by atmospheric oxygen
turns golden yellow when exposed to light
questions.explanation: NaOH is deliquescent: it absorbs moisture (and CO2) from the air.

questions.topic: Metals of the first transition series
questions.stem: To make coloured glasses, small quantities of oxides of metals which form coloured silicates are often added to the reaction mixture consisting of Na2CO3 and SiO2. Such a metal is
questions.explanation: Transition metals such as copper form coloured compounds (silicates); K, Ba and Zn compounds are colourless.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name for the hydrocarbon CH3-C(C2H5)=CH-CH(CH3)-CH3?
questions.explanation: The longest chain has 6 carbons including the ethyl group: CH3-CH(CH3)-CH=C(CH3)-CH2-CH3, with the double bond at C3 from either end. Lowest substituent locants give 2,4-dimethylhex-3-ene.

questions.stem: The label on a reagent bottle containing a clear organic liquid dropped off. The liquid was neutral to litmus and gave a colourless gas with metallic sodium. The liquid must be an
questions.explanation: Alkanols are neutral and react with sodium to liberate hydrogen; alkanoic acids would be acidic.

questions.stem: (COOH)2 + NaOH -> HOOC-COO^-Na^+ + H2O. The above reaction is an example of
questions.explanation: An acid (ethanedioic acid) reacts with a base to form a salt and water: neutralization.

questions.stem: Alkanoic acids have low volatility compared with alkanols because they
options: have two oxygen atoms while alkanols have one
form two hydrogen bonds while alkanols do not
form two hydrogen bonds while alkanols form one
questions.explanation: Alkanoic acid molecules pair up through two hydrogen bonds (dimers), whereas alkanol molecules form only one per link, so acids are less volatile.

questions.stem: The octane number of a fuel whose performance is the same as that of a mixture of 55 g of 2,2,4-trimethylpentane and 45 g of n-heptane is
questions.explanation: Octane number = percentage of 2,2,4-trimethylpentane (iso-octane) in its mixture with heptane: 55/100 = 55.

questions.stem: Which of the following is formed when maltose reacts with concentrated tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid?
questions.explanation: Concentrated H2SO4 dehydrates the sugar, leaving a black mass of carbon (sugar charcoal).

questions.stem: Which of the following can be obtained by fractional distillation?
options: Iodine from a solution of iodine in carbon tetrachloride
Sulphur from a solution of sulphur in carbon disulphide
questions.explanation: Liquid air is a mixture of liquids with different boiling points (N2 -196 °C, O2 -183 °C), separated by fractional distillation.

questions.stem: Which of the following are mixtures? I. Petroleum II. Rubber latex III. Vulcanizer's solution IV. Carbon (IV) sulphide
questions.explanation: Petroleum, latex and vulcanizer's solution (rubber in a solvent) are mixtures; carbon disulphide is a compound.

questions.stem: An iron ore is known to contain 70.0% Fe2O3. The mass of iron metal which can theoretically be obtained from 80 kg of the ore is [Fe = 56, O = 16]

In two separate experiments 0.36 g and 0.71 g of chlorine combine with a metal X to give Y and Z respectively. An analysis showed that Y and Z contain 0.20 g and 0.40 g of X respectively. The data above represent the law of
questions.explanation: The chlorine:X ratios are 0.36/0.20 = 1.8 and 0.71/0.40 = 1.78, essentially the same, so Y and Z are the same compound: the law of constant composition.

questions.stem: A given quantity of gas occupies a volume of 228 cm^3 at a pressure of 750 mm Hg. What will be its volume at atmospheric pressure?

Calculate the volume of carbon (IV) oxide measured at s.t.p produced when 1 kg of potassium hydrogen trioxocarbonate (IV) is totally decomposed by heat. [G.M.V at s.t.p = 22.4 dm^3, K = 39, O = 16, C = 12, H = 1]
questions.explanation: 2KHCO3 -> K2CO3 + H2O + CO2: 1000/100 = 10 mol KHCO3 gives 5 mol CO2, and 5 x 22.4 = 112 dm^3.

questions.stem: A sample of a gas exerts a pressure of 8.2 atm when confined in a 2.93 dm^3 container at 20 °C. The number of moles of gas in the sample is [R = 0.082 litre atm/deg mole]
Atoms of element X (with 2 electrons in the outer shell) combine with atoms of Y (with 7 electrons in the outer shell). Which of the following is FALSE? The compound formed
questions.explanation: X forms X^2+ and Y forms Y^-, so the formula is XY2, not XY.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: The ions X^- and Y^+ are isoelectronic, each containing a total of 10 electrons. How many protons are in the nuclei of the neutral atoms of X and Y respectively?
questions.explanation: X gained one electron, so it has 9 protons; Y lost one electron, so it has 11 protons.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: The electronic configuration of an element is 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^3. How many unpaired electrons are there in the element?
questions.explanation: By Hund's rule the three 3p electrons occupy separate orbitals singly, giving 3 unpaired electrons.

questions.stem: Which of the following represents the type of bonding present in ammonium chloride?
questions.explanation: NH4+ contains a dative (coordinate) bond from N to H+, and NH4+ and Cl- are held by an ionic bond.

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: Which of the following is arranged in order of increasing electronegativity?
questions.explanation: Electronegativity increases across period 3 from sodium to chlorine.

questions.stem: A quantity of air was passed through a weighed amount of alkaline pyrogallol. An increase in the weight of the pyrogallol would result from the absorption of
questions.explanation: Alkaline pyrogallol absorbs oxygen.

questions.stem: Which of the following ions is a pollutant in drinking water even in trace amounts?
questions.explanation: Mercury (II) ions are highly toxic heavy-metal ions even at trace levels.

questions.stem: The solubility of copper (II) tetraoxosulphate (VI) is 75 g in 100 g of water at 100 °C and 25 g in 100 g of water at 30 °C. What mass of the salt would crystallize if 50 g of copper (II) tetraoxosulphate (VI) solution saturated at 100 °C were cooled to 30 °C?
questions.explanation: 50 g of saturated solution holds 50 x 75/175 = 21.4 g salt in 28.6 g water; at 30 °C that water holds 7.1 g, so 14.3 g crystallizes.

questions.stem: A sample of temporary hard water can be prepared in the laboratory by
options: dissolving calcium chloride in distilled water
saturating lime water with carbon (IV) oxide
saturating distilled water with calcium hydroxide
dissolving sodium hydrogen trioxocarbonate (IV) in some distilled water
questions.explanation: Excess CO2 converts lime water into soluble calcium hydrogen trioxocarbonate (IV), the cause of temporary hardness.

questions.stem: A property of a colloidal dispersion which a solution does not have is
questions.explanation: Colloidal particles are large enough to scatter a beam of light (Tyndall effect); true solutions do not.

questions.stem: The volumes of some gases that dissolve in 1.0 cm^3 of water at 15 °C are: sulphur (IV) oxide 50 cm^3, ammonia 800 cm^3, hydrogen chloride 450 cm^3, carbon (IV) oxide 1.0 cm^3. Which of the following is suitable for demonstrating the fountain experiment?
questions.explanation: The fountain experiment needs extremely soluble gases; ammonia and hydrogen chloride are the most soluble.

questions.stem: What volume of CO2 at s.t.p would be obtained by reacting 10 cm^3 of 0.1 M solution of anhydrous sodium trioxocarbonate (IV) with excess acid? [G.M.V at s.t.p = 22.4 dm^3]
questions.explanation: Moles Na2CO3 = 0.010 x 0.1 = 0.001, giving 0.001 mol CO2 = 22.4 cm^3.

questions.stem: If a current of 1.5 A is passed for 4.00 hours through a molten tin salt and 13.3 g of tin is deposited, what is the oxidation state of the metal in the salt? [Sn = 118.7, F = 96500 C mol^-1]
Which of the following aqueous solutions, Na2CO3, Na2SO4, FeCl3, NH4Cl and CH3COONa, have pH greater than 7?
questions.explanation: Salts of a strong base and a weak acid (Na2CO3, CH3COONa) hydrolyse to give alkaline solutions; Na2SO4 is neutral and FeCl3 and NH4Cl are acidic.

questions.stem: MnO4^- + 8H^+ + ne^- -> Mn^2+ + 4H2O. What is the value of n in the reaction above?
questions.explanation: Mn goes from +7 to +2, gaining 5 electrons (charge check: -1 + 8 - 5 = +2).

questions.stem: 2H2S(g) + SO2(g) -> 3S(s) + 2H2O(l). The above reaction is
options: a redox reaction in which H2S is the oxidant and SO2 is the reductant
a redox reaction in which SO2 is the oxidant and H2S is the reductant
not a redox reaction because there is no oxidant in the reaction equation
not a redox reaction because there is no reductant in the reaction equation
questions.explanation: S in SO2 goes from +4 to 0 (reduced, so SO2 is the oxidant) while S in H2S goes from -2 to 0 (oxidised, so H2S is the reductant).

questions.stem: Manganese (IV) oxide is known to hasten the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide. Its main action is to
options: increase the surface area of the reactants
increase the concentration of the reactants
lower the activation energy for the reaction
lower the heat of reaction, ΔH, for the reaction
questions.explanation: MnO2 is a catalyst: it provides a pathway of lower activation energy without changing ΔH.

questions.stem: NO + CO <=> 1/2 N2 + CO2, ΔH = -89.3 kJ. What conditions would favour maximum conversion of nitrogen (II) oxide and carbon (II) oxide in the reaction above?
questions.explanation: The forward reaction is exothermic (favoured by low temperature) and reduces gas moles from 2 to 1.5 (favoured by high pressure).

questions.stem: Which of the following equilibria is unaffected by a pressure change?
questions.explanation: H2 + I2 <=> 2HI has 2 mol of gas on each side, so pressure does not shift it.

questions.stem: The rate of reaction of nitrogen (II) oxide with chlorine at 25 °C is as follows: initial [NO] = 0.001 mol, initial rate = 3.0 x 10^-5 mol/s; initial [NO] = 0.002 mol, initial rate = 1.2 x 10^-4 mol/s. It can be concluded that doubling the initial concentration of NO increases the rate of reaction by a factor of
Which of the following gases will rekindle a brightly glowing splint?
questions.explanation: Dinitrogen oxide decomposes at the hot splint, releasing oxygen that rekindles it.

questions.stem: Which of the following salts can be melted without decomposition?
questions.explanation: Sodium carbonate is thermally stable and melts without decomposing; the other carbonates give off CO2 on heating.

questions.stem: Oxygen gas can be prepared by heating
questions.explanation: 2KNO3 -> 2KNO2 + O2; the ammonium salts give N2O and N2 respectively.

questions.topic: Metals of the first transition series
questions.stem: Addition of aqueous ammonia to a solution of Zn^2+ gives a white precipitate which dissolves in an excess of ammonia because
options: zinc forms a complex which is readily soluble in excess ammonia
ammonia solution is a strong base
questions.explanation: Zn(OH)2 dissolves in excess ammonia by forming the soluble complex ion [Zn(NH3)4]^2+.

questions.stem: Which of the following, in clear solution, forms a white precipitate when carbon (IV) oxide is bubbled into it for a short time?
questions.explanation: Lime water turns milky as insoluble CaCO3 forms.

questions.stem: Copper (II) tetraoxosulphate (VI) is widely used as a
questions.explanation: CuSO4 (for example in Bordeaux mixture) is used as a fungicide.

questions.stem: Which of the following metals can be prepared by the thermal decomposition of their trioxonitrate (V) salts?
questions.explanation: Nitrates of the least reactive metals (Hg, Ag) decompose all the way to the metal; copper and magnesium nitrates give the oxides.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds can exist as geometric isomers?
questions.explanation: But-2-ene has two different groups on each doubly bonded carbon, so it has cis and trans forms.

questions.stem: How many structural isomers can be written for the alkyl bromide C4H9Br?
questions.explanation: The four isomers are 1-bromobutane, 2-bromobutane, 1-bromo-2-methylpropane and 2-bromo-2-methylpropane. (The paper misprints the formula as C2H9Br.)

questions.stem: How many grams of bromine will be required to completely react with 10 g of propyne? [C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80]
questions.explanation: Propyne (C3H4 = 40) adds 2 Br2 per molecule: 10/40 = 0.25 mol needs 0.5 mol Br2 = 80 g.

questions.stem: Ethene, when passed into concentrated H2SO4, is rapidly absorbed. The product is diluted with water and then warmed to produce
questions.explanation: Ethene forms ethyl hydrogen sulphate, which is hydrolysed by water on warming to ethanol.

questions.stem: One of the advantages of detergents over soap is that detergents
options: form soluble salts with hard water
are able to deter germs more than soap
questions.explanation: The calcium and magnesium salts of detergents are soluble, so detergents do not form scum in hard water.

questions.stem: CH3CH2CHXCH3 (X = halogen) + alc. KOH -> CH3CH=CHCH3 + CH3CH2CH=CH2. The above reaction is an example of
questions.explanation: Alcoholic KOH removes HX from the haloalkane to form alkenes: dehydrohalogenation.

questions.stem: The compound CH3-CH(CH3)-CH2Cl is known as
questions.explanation: The longest chain is 3 carbons, with Cl on C1 and a methyl group on C2: 1-chloro-2-methylpropane.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE of the complete hydrolysis of a glyceride by sodium hydroxide?
options: 3 moles of NaOH are required for each mole of glyceride
only one mole of soap is formed
concentrated H2SO4 is essential for the completion of the reaction
questions.explanation: A triglyceride has three ester links, so it needs 3 mol NaOH and gives 3 mol soap and 1 mol glycerol.

questions.stem: Which of the following are the products of the reaction between CH3COOH and Cl2 in sunlight?
questions.explanation: In sunlight chlorine substitutes a hydrogen of the methyl group, giving chloroethanoic acid and HCl.

questions.stem: Which of the following substances is not a homogeneous mixture?
questions.explanation: Flood water carries suspended mud and debris, so its composition is not uniform; the others are uniform solutions.

questions.stem: There is a large temperature interval between the melting point and the boiling point of a metal because
options: metals have very high melting points
melting does not break the metallic bond but boiling does
the crystal lattice of metals is easily broken
questions.explanation: Melting only loosens the lattice while metallic bonding persists in the liquid; boiling must break the metallic bonds, which needs much more energy.

questions.stem: How many moles of [H+] are there in 1 dm^3 of 0.5 M solution of H2SO4?
questions.explanation: H2SO4 is dibasic: 0.5 mol of acid releases 2 x 0.5 = 1.0 mol of H+.

questions.stem: wH2SO4 + xAl(OH)3 → yH2O + zAl2(SO4)3. The respective values of w, x, y and z in the equation above are
questions.explanation: Balanced: 3H2SO4 + 2Al(OH)3 → 6H2O + Al2(SO4)3.

questions.stem: A given mass of gas occupies 2 dm^3 at 300 K. At what temperature will its volume be doubled keeping the pressure constant?
questions.explanation: Charles' law: V/T is constant, so doubling V doubles T to 600 K.

questions.stem: If 100 cm^3 of oxygen pass through a porous plug in 50 seconds, the time taken for the same volume of hydrogen to pass through the same porous plug is [O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: Graham's law: t(H2) = 50 x sqrt(2/32) = 50/4 = 12.5 s.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the molecules of a substance?
questions.explanation: Absolute temperature is proportional to the average kinetic energy of the molecules.

questions.stem: An increase in temperature causes an increase in the pressure of a gas in a fixed volume due to an increase in the
options: number of molecules of the gas
number of collisions between the gas molecules
number of collisions between the gas molecules and the walls of the container
questions.explanation: Faster molecules hit the container walls more often and harder; gas pressure comes from these wall collisions.

questions.stem: How many lone pairs of electrons are there on the central atom of the H2O molecule?
questions.explanation: Oxygen has 6 valence electrons; two form O-H bonds, leaving two lone pairs.

questions.stem: 14/7 N + X → 17/8 O + 1/1 H. In the above reaction, X is a
questions.explanation: Mass: 14 + 4 = 17 + 1; charge: 7 + 2 = 8 + 1, so X is 4/2 He (an alpha particle).

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: Four elements P, Q, R and S have 1, 2, 3 and 7 electrons in their outermost shells respectively. The element which is unlikely to be a metal is
questions.explanation: An element with 7 outer electrons readily gains one electron (a halogen), so it is a non-metal.

questions.stem: The pollutants that are likely to be present in an industrial environment are
options: H2S, SO2 and oxides of nitrogen
questions.explanation: Industrial fuel burning and processing release H2S, SO2 and oxides of nitrogen.

questions.stem: Which of the following gases dissolves in water vapour to produce acid rain during rainfall?
questions.explanation: SO2 dissolves to form trioxosulphate(IV) acid, a major cause of acid rain.

questions.stem: Water for town supply is chlorinated to make it free from
questions.explanation: Chlorine is added as a disinfectant to kill bacteria.

questions.stem: On which of the following is the solubility of a gaseous substance dependent? I. Nature of solvent. II. Nature of solute. III. Temperature. IV. Pressure.
questions.explanation: Gas solubility depends on the solvent and solute, decreases as temperature rises and increases with pressure (Henry's law).

questions.stem: An emulsion paint consists of
options: gas or liquid particles dispersed in liquid
questions.explanation: An emulsion is a colloid of liquid droplets dispersed in another liquid.

questions.stem: A sample of orange juice is found to have a pH of 3.80. What is the concentration of the hydroxide ion in the juice?
Arrange HCl, CH3COOH, C6H5CH3 in order of increasing conductivity.
questions.explanation: Methylbenzene is a non-electrolyte, ethanoic acid a weak electrolyte and HCl a strong electrolyte.

questions.stem: Which of these is an acid salt?
questions.explanation: NaHS still contains a replaceable hydrogen, so it is an acid salt; the others are double, basic and mixed salts.

questions.stem: How many grams of H2SO4 are necessary for the preparation of 0.175 dm^3 of 6.00 M H2SO4? [S = 32.06, O = 16.00, H = 1.00]
Copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution is electrolyzed using carbon electrodes. Which of the following are produced at the anode and cathode respectively?
questions.explanation: With inert electrodes, OH- is discharged at the anode (oxygen) and Cu2+ at the cathode (copper).

questions.stem: Calculate the mass, in kilograms, of magnesium produced by the electrolysis of magnesium(II) chloride in a cell operating for 24 hours at 500 amperes. [Faraday = 96,500 C mol^-1, Mg = 24]
MnO2 + 2Cl- + 4H+ → Mn2+ + Cl2 + 2H2O. The changes in oxidation numbers when the manganese, chlorine and hydrogen ions react according to the above equation are respectively
questions.explanation: Mn goes from +4 to +2 (-2), Cl from -1 to 0 (+1), and H stays +1 (0).

questions.stem: 2S2O3^2- + I2 → S4O6^2- + 2I-. In the reaction above, the oxidizing agent is
questions.explanation: I2 gains electrons (is reduced to I-), so it is the oxidizing agent.

questions.stem: In which of the following is the entropy change positive?
questions.explanation: Changing liquid to gas greatly increases disorder, so the entropy change is positive.

questions.stem: In what way is the equilibrium constant for the forward reaction related to that of the reverse reaction?
options: The addition of the two is expected to be one
The product of the two is expected to be one
The two equilibrium constants are identical
The product of the two is always greater than one
questions.explanation: K(reverse) = 1/K(forward), so their product is one.

questions.stem: Which of the following equilibria shows little or no net reaction when the volume of the system is decreased?
questions.explanation: There are equal moles of gas (2) on both sides, so a pressure change does not shift the equilibrium.

questions.stem: For a general equation of the nature xP + yQ ⇌ mR + nS, the expression for the equilibrium constant is
questions.explanation: K = product concentrations raised to their coefficients divided by reactant concentrations raised to theirs.

questions.stem: Which of these statements is TRUE about carbon(IV) oxide?
options: It is strongly acidic in water
It is very soluble in water
It supports the burning of magnesium to produce magnesium oxide
questions.explanation: Burning magnesium is hot enough to decompose CO2, forming MgO and carbon; CO2 does not generally support combustion.

questions.stem: Which of the following combinations of gases is used for metal welding? I. Oxygen and ethyne. II. Hydrogen and ethyne. III. Hydrogen and oxygen. IV. Ethyne, hydrogen and oxygen.
questions.explanation: The oxy-acetylene (oxygen/ethyne) and oxy-hydrogen flames are used for welding.

questions.stem: Which of the following oxides of nitrogen is unstable in air?
questions.explanation: NO combines immediately with atmospheric oxygen to form brown NO2.

questions.stem: The gas formed when ammonium trioxonitrate(V) is heated with sodium hydroxide is
questions.explanation: Ammonium salts warmed with an alkali liberate ammonia.

questions.stem: Safety matches contain sulphur and
questions.explanation: The head of a safety match contains potassium trioxochlorate(V) (an oxidant) with sulphur; red phosphorus is on the striking surface.

questions.stem: Sodium hydroxide solution can be conveniently stored in a container made of
questions.explanation: Lead, zinc and aluminium are amphoteric and are attacked by NaOH; copper is not.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT used as raw material in the Solvay process?
questions.explanation: Sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) is the product of the Solvay process, not a raw material.

questions.stem: Duralumin consists of aluminium, copper,
questions.explanation: Duralumin is aluminium alloyed with copper, manganese and magnesium.

questions.stem: CaO(s) + H2O(l) → Ca(OH)2(s), ΔH = -65 kJ. The process represented by the above equation is known as
questions.explanation: Adding water to quicklime to form slaked lime is called slaking.

questions.stem: The carbon atoms in ethane are
questions.explanation: Each carbon in ethane forms four single (sigma) bonds, so it is sp^3 hybridized.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds is a secondary alkanol?
questions.explanation: In butan-2-ol the OH carbon is bonded to two other carbons, so it is secondary; (CH3)3COH is tertiary and the third is primary.

questions.stem: Which of the following are isomers?
questions.explanation: Ethanol and dimethyl ether both have the formula C2H6O but different structures.

questions.stem: The functional group present in an organic compound that liberates a gas on treatment with a saturated solution of NaHCO3 is
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with NaHCO3 to liberate CO2.

questions.stem: The characteristic reaction of carbonyl compounds is
questions.explanation: The polar C=O bond undergoes nucleophilic addition.

questions.stem: An organic compound containing 40.1% carbon and 6.667% hydrogen has an empirical formula of
Alkanals can be differentiated from alkanones by reaction with
questions.explanation: Alkanals reduce Tollens' reagent to a silver mirror; alkanones do not. The other reagents react with both.

questions.stem: An example of a polysaccharide is
questions.explanation: Starch is a polymer of glucose units; the others are monosaccharides.

questions.stem: The dissolution of common salt in water is a physical change because
options: the salt can be obtained by crystallization
the salt can be recovered by the evaporation of water
heat is not generated during mixing
the solution will not boil at 100 °C
questions.explanation: No new substance is formed: simply evaporating the water recovers the salt unchanged.

questions.stem: Which of the following substances is a mixture?
questions.explanation: Bronze is an alloy (a mixture of copper and tin); the others are an element or pure compounds.

questions.stem: How many moles of oxygen molecules would be produced from the decomposition of 2.5 moles of potassium trioxochlorate(V)?
questions.explanation: 2KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2, so 2.5 mol KClO3 gives 2.5 x 3/2 = 3.75 mol O2.

questions.stem: A balanced chemical equation obeys the law of
questions.explanation: Balancing makes the number of each kind of atom, and hence the mass, equal on both sides.

questions.stem: At 25 °C and 1 atm, a gas occupies a volume of 1.50 dm^3. What volume will it occupy at 100 °C and 1 atm?
questions.explanation: V2 = 1.50 x 373/298 = 1.88 dm^3 (Charles' law, using kelvin temperatures).

questions.stem: A gaseous mixture of 80.0 g of oxygen and 56.0 g of nitrogen has a total pressure of 1.8 atm. The partial pressure of oxygen in the mixture is [O = 16, N = 14]
For iodine crystals to sublime on heating, the molecules must acquire energy that is
options: less than the forces of attraction in the solid
equal to the forces of attraction in the solid
greater than the forces of attraction in both the solid and the liquid phases
questions.explanation: Sublimation takes molecules straight from solid to vapour, so their energy must overcome the attractions holding both condensed phases together.

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: An element, E, has the electronic configuration 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^3. The reaction of E with a halogen X can give
questions.explanation: E is phosphorus (group V), which forms both PX3 and PX5 (e.g. PCl3 and PCl5).

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: Two atoms represented as 235/92 U and 238/92 U are
questions.explanation: They have the same atomic number (92) but different mass numbers, so they are isotopes.

questions.stem: As the difference in electronegativity between bonded atoms increases, the polarity of the bond
questions.explanation: A larger electronegativity difference makes the electron pair shift more, so the bond becomes more polar.

questions.stem: Which group of elements forms hydrides that are pyramidal in structure?
questions.explanation: Group V hydrides (NH3, PH3) have three bond pairs and one lone pair, giving a pyramidal shape.

questions.stem: Water has a rather high boiling point despite its low molecular mass because of the presence of
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonds between water molecules need extra energy to break.

questions.topic: Air as a mixture and uses of noble gases
questions.stem: Argon is used in gas-filled electric lamps because it helps to
options: prevent the reduction of the lamp filament
prevent oxidation of the lamp filament
keep the atmosphere in the lamp inert
questions.explanation: Unreactive argon surrounds the hot tungsten filament so that it is not oxidized (burnt out).

questions.stem: Water can be identified by the use of
questions.explanation: Water turns white anhydrous CuSO4 blue.

questions.stem: The phenomenon whereby sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) decahydrate loses some of its water of crystallization on exposure to the atmosphere is known as
questions.explanation: Losing water of crystallization to the air is efflorescence.

questions.stem: A student prepares 0.5 M solutions each of hydrochloric and ethanoic acids and then measures their pH. The result would show that the
options: sum of the pH values is 14
ethanoic acid solution has a higher pH
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid is weak and only partly ionized, so its [H+] is lower and its pH higher.

questions.stem: NH3 + H3O+ → NH4+ + H2O. It may be deduced from the reaction above that
options: H3O+ acts as an oxidizing agent
questions.explanation: H3O+ donates a proton to NH3, so it acts as a (Bronsted-Lowry) acid; no oxidation numbers change.

questions.stem: 4.0 g of sodium hydroxide in 250 cm^3 of solution contains

Half-cell reactions and E° values: Cu2+(aq) + 2e- → Cu(s), +0.34 V; Fe2+(aq) + 2e- → Fe(s), -0.44 V; Ba2+(aq) + 2e- → Ba(s), -2.90 V; Zn2+(aq) + 2e- → Zn(s), -0.76 V. From the data above, it can be deduced that the most powerful reducing agent of the four metals is
questions.explanation: The metal with the most negative electrode potential (Ba, -2.90 V) loses electrons most readily.

questions.stem: The oxidation states of chlorine in HOCl, HClO3 and HClO4 are respectively
questions.explanation: With H = +1 and O = -2: HOCl gives Cl = +1, HClO3 gives +5, HClO4 gives +7.

questions.stem: A reaction takes place spontaneously if
questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS is negative (spontaneous) when ΔH < TΔS.

questions.stem: The standard enthalpies of formation of CO2(g), H2O(g) and CO(g) in kJ mol^-1 are -394, -242 and -110 respectively. What is the standard enthalpy change for the reaction CO(g) + H2O(g) → CO2(g) + H2(g)?
10 g of a solid is in equilibrium with its own vapour. When 1 g of a small amount of solid is added, the vapour pressure
questions.explanation: Vapour pressure depends only on temperature, not on the amount of solid present.

questions.stem: NaCl(s) + H2SO4(l) → HCl(g) + NaHSO4(s). In the reaction above, H2SO4 behaves as
questions.explanation: The concentrated acid donates a proton to chloride, displacing the more volatile HCl; there is no redox or dehydration.

questions.stem: Which of these salts will produce its metal, oxygen and nitrogen(IV) oxide on heating?
questions.explanation: 2AgNO3 → 2Ag + 2NO2 + O2; nitrates of less reactive metals decompose to the metal.

questions.stem: An experiment produces a gaseous mixture of carbon(IV) oxide and carbon(II) oxide. In order to obtain pure carbon(II) oxide, the gas mixture should be
questions.explanation: NaOH absorbs the acidic CO2, leaving the neutral CO.

questions.stem: When dilute aqueous solutions of lead(II) nitrate and potassium bromide are mixed, a precipitate is observed. The products of this reaction are
questions.explanation: Double decomposition: insoluble PbBr2 precipitates while K+ and NO3- remain in solution.

questions.stem: Copper metal will react with concentrated trioxonitrate(V) acid to give
questions.explanation: Cu + 4HNO3(conc) → Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO2 + 2H2O; NO forms with the dilute acid.

questions.stem: The active reducing agent in the blast furnace for the extraction of iron is
questions.explanation: CO reduces the iron oxide: Fe2O3 + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO2.

questions.stem: Al2O3(s) + 3H2SO4(aq) → Al2(SO4)3(aq) + 3H2O(l); Al2O3(s) + 2NaOH(aq) + 3H2O(l) → 2NaAl(OH)4(aq). We can conclude from the equations above that Al2O3(s) is
questions.explanation: It reacts with both an acid and a base, so it is amphoteric.

questions.stem: H2N-CH2-COOH. The two functional groups in the above compound are
questions.explanation: -NH2 is an amine group and -COOH a carboxylic acid group (an amino acid).

questions.stem: The fraction of crude oil used as jet fuel is
questions.explanation: Kerosene is the fraction used as aviation (jet) fuel.

questions.stem: CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH(CH3)CH2CH3. The IUPAC nomenclature for the compound above is
questions.explanation: The longest chain has six carbons with methyl groups on C-2 and C-4: 2,4-dimethylhexane.

questions.stem: It is not desirable to use lead tetraethyl as an anti-knock agent because
options: of pollution effects from the exhaust fumes
it lowers the octane rating of petrol
questions.explanation: Leaded petrol releases toxic lead compounds into the air.

questions.stem: The carbon atoms in ethane are
questions.explanation: Each carbon in ethane forms four single bonds, so it is sp^3 hybridized.

questions.stem: Catalytic hydrogenation of benzene produces
questions.explanation: Adding three moles of H2 to benzene over Ni gives cyclohexane, C6H12.

questions.stem: CH3COOCH2CH3 and CH3CH2CH2COOH are
questions.explanation: Ethyl ethanoate and butanoic acid both have the molecular formula C4H8O2, so they are (functional group) isomers.

questions.stem: Palm wine turns sour with time because
options: the sugar content is converted into alcohol
the carbon(IV) oxide formed during the fermentation process has a sour taste
it is commonly adulterated by the tappers and sellers
microbial activity results in the production of organic acids within it
questions.explanation: Micro-organisms oxidize the alcohol to ethanoic and other organic acids, which taste sour.

questions.stem: Which of these represents saponification?
options: reaction of carboxylic acids with sodium hydroxide
reaction of carboxylic acids with alcohols
reaction of alkanoates with sodium hydroxide
questions.explanation: Saponification is alkaline hydrolysis of an ester (alkanoate), e.g. a fat with NaOH to give soap.

questions.stem: The confirmatory test for alkanoic acids in organic qualitative analysis is the
options: turning of wet blue litmus paper red
reaction with alkanols to form esters
reaction with sodium hydroxide to form salt and water
reaction with aqueous Na2CO3 to liberate a gas which turns lime water milky
questions.explanation: Alkanoic acids liberate CO2 from trioxocarbonates(IV); phenols and other weak acids do not.

questions.stem: A mixture of sand, ammonium chloride and sodium chloride is best separated by
options: sublimation followed by addition of water and filtration
sublimation followed by addition of water and evaporation
addition of water followed by filtration and sublimation
addition of water followed by crystallization and sublimation
questions.explanation: Heating first sublimes off NH4Cl; water then dissolves NaCl so the sand can be filtered off (the filtrate is evaporated to recover NaCl).

questions.stem: A pure solid usually melts
options: over a wide range of temperature
over a narrow range of temperature
at a lower temperature than the impure one
at the same temperature as the impure one
questions.explanation: A pure solid has a sharp melting point; impurities lower it and broaden the range.

questions.stem: At the same temperature and pressure, 50 cm^3 of nitrogen gas contains the same number of molecules as
questions.explanation: Avogadro's law: equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules.

questions.stem: 8 g of CH4 occupies 11.2 dm^3 at s.t.p. What volume would 22 g of CH3CH2CH3 occupy under the same conditions? [C = 12, H = 1]
questions.explanation: 8 g CH4 is 0.5 mol; 22 g of propane (M = 44) is also 0.5 mol, so it occupies 11.2 dm^3.

questions.stem: To what temperature must a gas at 273 K be heated in order to double both its volume and pressure?
questions.explanation: PV/T is constant: doubling both P and V multiplies T by 4, giving 4 x 273 = 1092 K.

questions.stem: For a gas, the relative molecular mass is equal to 2Y. What is Y?
options: The vapour density of the gas
questions.explanation: Relative molecular mass = 2 x vapour density.

questions.stem: The densities of two gases, X and Y, are 0.5 g dm^-3 and 2.0 g dm^-3 respectively. What is the rate of diffusion of X relative to Y?
questions.explanation: Graham's law: rate X/rate Y = sqrt(2.0/0.5) = sqrt(4) = 2.0.

questions.stem: An increase in temperature causes an increase in the pressure of a gas because
options: it decreases the number of collisions between the molecules
the molecules of the gas bombard the walls of the container more frequently
it increases the number of collisions between the molecules
it causes the molecules to combine
questions.explanation: Pressure arises from molecular impacts on the walls, which become more frequent and forceful as temperature rises.

questions.stem: The shape of ammonia molecules is
questions.explanation: NH3 has four electron pairs (three bonding, one lone) arranged tetrahedrally; the atoms form a pyramid within this tetrahedral arrangement. None of the other shapes fits.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: The number of electrons in the valence shell of an element of atomic number 14 is
questions.explanation: Z = 14 gives the configuration 2, 8, 4, so there are 4 valence electrons.

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: Which of the following physical properties decreases down a group in the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Down a group the outer electrons are further from the nucleus, so electronegativity decreases while radii and electropositivity increase.

questions.stem: Elements X, Y and Z belong to groups I, V and VII respectively. Which of the following is TRUE about the bond types of XZ and YZ3?
options: XZ is electrovalent and YZ3 is covalent
XZ is covalent and YZ3 is electrovalent
questions.explanation: A group I metal and a halogen form an ionic compound (like NaCl); a group V non-metal and a halogen form a covalent molecule (like PCl3).

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: Which of the following atoms represents deuterium? (number of protons, neutrons, electrons)
questions.explanation: Deuterium (2/1 H) has 1 proton, 1 neutron and 1 electron.

questions.stem: A solid that absorbs water from the atmosphere and forms an aqueous solution is
questions.explanation: A deliquescent solid absorbs so much moisture that it dissolves to form a solution.

questions.stem: A major effect of oil pollution in coastal water is the
options: increase in the acidity of the water
questions.explanation: An oil film cuts off oxygen and coats organisms, killing marine life.

questions.stem: Sodium chloride has no solubility product value because of its
questions.explanation: Solubility products are used only for sparingly soluble salts; NaCl is highly soluble.

questions.stem: The solubility in moles per dm^3 of 20.2 g of potassium trioxonitrate(V) dissolved in 100 g of water at room temperature is [K = 39, O = 16, N = 14]
questions.explanation: M(KNO3) = 101, so 20.2 g = 0.2 mol per 100 g of water, i.e. 2.00 mol per 1000 g (about 1 dm^3).

questions.stem: A few drops of concentrated HCl are added to about 10 cm^3 of a solution of pH 3.4. The pH of the resulting mixture is
options: the same as that of pure water
questions.explanation: Adding strong acid raises [H+], so the pH falls below 3.4.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds is a base?
questions.explanation: CaO is a metallic oxide that neutralizes acids to form salt and water; the others are acidic.

questions.stem: 20 cm^3 of a 2.0 M solution of ethanoic acid was added to excess of 0.05 M sodium hydroxide. The mass of the salt produced is [Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: Moles of acid = 0.020 x 2.0 = 0.040 mol, giving 0.040 mol CH3COONa (M = 82): 0.040 x 82 = 3.28 g.

questions.stem: What volume of oxygen measured at s.t.p. would be liberated on electrolysis by 9650 coulombs of electricity? [Molar volume of gas = 22.4 dm^3, F = 96,500 C mol^-1]
Crude copper could be purified by the electrolysis of concentrated copper(II) chloride if the crude copper is
options: made both the anode and the cathode
questions.explanation: The impure copper anode dissolves and pure copper is deposited on the cathode.

questions.stem: H-(s) + H2O(l) → H2(g) + OH-(aq). From the equation above, it can be inferred that the
options: hydride ion is a reducing agent
hydride ion is an oxidizing agent
questions.explanation: The hydride ion is oxidized from -1 to 0 (in H2), donating electrons, so it is the reducing agent.

questions.stem: An anhydride is an oxide of a non-metal
options: which will not dissolve in water
whose solution in water has a pH greater than 7
whose solution in water has a pH less than 7
whose solution in water has a pH of 7
questions.explanation: An acid anhydride dissolves in water to form an acid, so the solution has pH below 7.

questions.stem: MnO4-(aq) + 8H+(aq) + 5Fe2+(aq) → Mn2+(aq) + 5Fe3+(aq) + 4H2O(l). The oxidation number of manganese in the above reaction changes from
questions.explanation: In MnO4-: Mn + 4(-2) = -1 gives Mn = +7; it ends as Mn2+ (+2).

questions.stem: Which of the following is TRUE of Le Chatelier's principle for an exothermic reaction?
options: Increase in temperature will cause an increase in the equilibrium constant
Increase in temperature will cause a decrease in the equilibrium constant
Addition of a catalyst will cause an increase in the equilibrium constant
Addition of a catalyst will cause a decrease in the equilibrium constant
questions.explanation: Raising the temperature favours the endothermic (backward) reaction, so K for an exothermic reaction falls; a catalyst does not change K.

questions.stem: Which of the following are produced when ammonium trioxonitrate(V) crystals are cautiously heated in a hard glass round-bottomed flask?
questions.explanation: NH4NO3 → N2O + 2H2O on gentle heating.

questions.stem: Which of these metals CANNOT replace hydrogen from alkaline solutions?
questions.explanation: Aluminium, zinc and tin are amphoteric and liberate hydrogen from alkalis; iron does not.

questions.stem: Clothes should be properly rinsed with water after bleaching because
options: chlorine reacts with fabrics during bleaching
the clothes are sterilized during bleaching
hydrogen chloride solution is produced during bleaching
questions.explanation: Chlorine bleaching (HOCl → HCl + [O]) leaves hydrochloric acid, which would weaken the fabric if not rinsed out.

questions.stem: Which of these solutions will give a white precipitate with a solution of barium chloride acidified with hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Only BaSO4 is insoluble in the acid; barium trioxocarbonate(IV) and trioxosulphate(IV) dissolve in HCl.

questions.stem: SO3 is NOT directly dissolved in water in the preparation of H2SO4 by the contact process because
options: the reaction between SO3 and water is violently exothermic
acid is usually added to water and never water to acid
SO3 does not dissolve in water readily
questions.explanation: SO3 reacts so exothermically with water that it forms a corrosive acid mist; it is absorbed in concentrated H2SO4 instead.

questions.stem: In an electrolytic set-up to protect iron from corrosion, the iron is
options: used with a metal of lower electropositive potential
questions.explanation: In cathodic protection the iron is made the cathode so it cannot lose electrons (rust).

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT true of metals?
options: They are good conductors of electricity
questions.explanation: Metallic oxides are generally basic (or amphoteric), not acidic.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct order of decreasing activity of the metals Fe, Ca, Al and Na?
questions.explanation: In the activity series Na is above Ca, which is above Al, which is above Fe.

questions.stem: When sodium is added to ethanol, the products are
questions.explanation: 2C2H5OH + 2Na → 2C2H5ONa + H2.

questions.stem: The general formula of alkanones is
questions.explanation: An alkanone has a carbonyl group bonded to two alkyl groups: R2CO.

questions.stem: One mole of a hydrocarbon contains 48 g of carbon. If its vapour density is 28, the hydrocarbon is [C = 12, H = 1]
questions.explanation: M = 2 x 28 = 56; 48 g C = 4 C atoms and 8 g H = 8 H atoms, giving C4H8 (CnH2n), an alkene.

questions.stem: Which of the following orbitals of carbon are mixed with hydrogen in methane?
questions.explanation: Carbon's 2s and three 2p orbitals hybridize to sp^3 orbitals, which overlap with hydrogen 1s orbitals.

questions.stem: Which of the following reagents will confirm the presence of unsaturation in a compound?
questions.explanation: Unsaturated compounds decolourize bromine water by addition across the multiple bond.

questions.stem: Chromatography is used to separate components of mixtures which differ in their rates of
questions.explanation: Components move (migrate) through the stationary phase at different rates because they are adsorbed to different extents.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of chemical change?
questions.explanation: Rusting forms a new substance (hydrated iron(III) oxide) and is not easily reversed.

questions.stem: What volume of oxygen will remain after reacting 8 cm^3 of hydrogen with 20 cm^3 of oxygen?
questions.explanation: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O: 8 cm^3 of H2 uses 4 cm^3 of O2, leaving 20 - 4 = 16 cm^3.

questions.stem: A gas sample with an initial volume of 3.25 dm^3 is heated and allowed to expand to 9.75 dm^3 at constant pressure. What is the ratio of the final absolute temperature to the initial absolute temperature?
questions.explanation: At constant pressure T2/T1 = V2/V1 = 9.75/3.25 = 3, so 3:1.

questions.stem: Two cylinders A and B each contain 30 cm^3 of oxygen and nitrogen respectively at the same temperature and pressure. If there are 5.0 moles of nitrogen, then the mass of oxygen is
questions.explanation: Equal volumes contain equal moles (Avogadro), so there are 5.0 mol O2 = 5.0 x 32 = 160.0 g.

questions.stem: A liquid begins to boil when
options: its vapour pressure is equal to the vapour pressure of its solid at the given temperature
molecules start escaping from its surface
its vapour pressure equals the atmospheric pressure
questions.explanation: Boiling occurs when the saturated vapour pressure equals the external (atmospheric) pressure.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: A particle that contains 8 protons, 9 neutrons and 7 electrons could be written as
questions.explanation: 8 protons makes it oxygen (Z = 8); mass number = 8 + 9 = 17; one electron fewer than protons gives a charge of +1.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: In the oil drop experiment, Millikan determined the
options: charge to mass ratio of the electron
questions.explanation: Millikan's oil drop experiment measured the charge on the electron.

questions.stem: The stability of ionic solids is generally due to the
options: negative electron affinity of most atoms
questions.explanation: Strong electrostatic attractions throughout the crystal lattice (lattice energy) stabilize ionic solids.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: Which of the following statements is FALSE about isotopes of the same element?
options: They have the same number of electrons in their outermost shells
They have the same atomic number and the same number of electrons
They have the same atomic number but different numbers of electrons
questions.explanation: Isotopes differ only in the number of neutrons; their electron numbers are the same.

questions.topic: Air as a mixture and uses of noble gases
questions.stem: Helium is often used in observation balloons because it is
questions.explanation: Helium is much less dense than air and, being a noble gas, does not burn.

questions.stem: Deliquescent substances are also
questions.explanation: Deliquescent substances absorb moisture from the air, so they are also hygroscopic.

questions.stem: The difference between colloids and suspensions is brought out clearly by the fact that while colloids
options: do not scatter light, suspensions cannot be so separated
can be separated by filtration, suspensions cannot be separated
can be separated by a membrane, suspensions cannot
do not settle out on standing, suspensions do
questions.explanation: Colloidal particles are small enough to stay dispersed, whereas suspended particles settle on standing.

questions.stem: In general, an increase in temperature increases the solubility of a solute in water because
options: more solute molecules collide with each other
most solutes dissolve with the evolution of heat
more solute molecules dissociate at higher temperature
most solutes dissolve with absorption of heat
questions.explanation: For endothermic dissolution, Le Chatelier's principle predicts that raising the temperature increases solubility.

questions.stem: Neutralization involves a reaction between H3O+ and
questions.explanation: H3O+ + OH- → 2H2O is the essential neutralization reaction.

questions.stem: Which of the following solutions will have a pH < 7?
questions.explanation: NH4Cl is a salt of a strong acid and a weak base; NH4+ hydrolyzes to give an acidic solution.

questions.stem: What is the pH of a 2.50 x 10^-5 M solution of sodium hydroxide?
In the process of silver-plating a metal M, the metal M is the
options: anode and a direct current is used
cathode and an alternating current is used
anode and an alternating current is used
cathode and a direct current is used
questions.explanation: Silver is deposited on the cathode, so the object is made the cathode in a d.c. circuit.

questions.stem: How many moles of copper would be deposited by passing 3 F of electricity through a solution of copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI)? (F = 96 500 C mol^-1)
questions.explanation: Cu2+ + 2e- → Cu, so 2 F deposit 1 mol; 3 F deposit 1.5 mol.

questions.stem: 2Cl-(aq) → Cl2(g) + 2e-. The above half-cell reaction occurring at the anode during the electrolysis of dilute ZnCl2 solution is
questions.explanation: Chloride ions lose electrons, which is oxidation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a redox reaction?
questions.explanation: Fe is oxidized from +2 to +3 while Br2 is reduced from 0 to -1; the others involve no change in oxidation number.

questions.stem: Cr2O7^2-(aq) + 14H+(aq) + 6I-(aq) → 2Cr3+(aq) + 3I2 + 7H2O(l). The change in the oxidation number of oxygen in the equation above is
questions.explanation: Oxygen is -2 both in Cr2O7^2- and in H2O, so there is no change.

questions.stem: If an equilibrium reaction has ΔH < 0, the reaction will proceed favourably in the forward direction at
questions.explanation: For an exothermic forward reaction, lowering the temperature shifts the equilibrium forward.

questions.stem: Which of the following processes leads to an increase in entropy?
options: Mixing a sample of NaCl and sand
questions.explanation: Boiling converts liquid to gas, a large increase in disorder; condensation and cooling decrease entropy.

questions.stem: Which of the following equilibria is shifted to the right as a result of an increase in pressure?
questions.explanation: Increased pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles: 2 mol NO2 → 1 mol N2O4.

questions.stem: In the industrial production of hydrogen from natural gas, carbon(IV) oxide produced along with the hydrogen is removed by
options: passing the mixture into lime water
questions.explanation: CO2 is much more soluble than H2 in water under pressure, so it is removed by washing the gas mixture under pressure.

questions.stem: Sulphur exists in six forms in the solid state. This property is known as
questions.explanation: Existence of an element in different forms in the same physical state is allotropy.

questions.stem: A gas that will turn orange potassium heptaoxodichromate(VI) solution to clear green is
questions.explanation: SO2 reduces acidified dichromate to green Cr3+ giving a clear solution; H2S also turns it green but deposits yellow sulphur, so the solution is not clear.

questions.stem: Which of the following ions will give a white precipitate with aqueous NaOH which is soluble in excess of the base?
questions.explanation: Zn(OH)2 is amphoteric and dissolves in excess NaOH; Ca(OH)2 and Mg(OH)2 do not, and Cu(OH)2 is blue.

questions.stem: In the extraction of iron in the blast furnace, limestone is used to
questions.explanation: Limestone decomposes to CaO, which combines with silica impurities to form slag.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds will impart a brick-red colour to a non-luminous Bunsen flame?
questions.explanation: Calcium gives a brick-red flame; sodium is golden yellow and lithium crimson.

questions.stem: Group IA metals are not found free in nature because they
options: are of low melting and boiling points
questions.explanation: Alkali metals are so reactive that they occur only as compounds.

questions.stem: CH3COOH + CH3CH2OH (conc. H2SO4) → X + Y. X and Y in the reaction above are respectively
questions.explanation: Esterification gives ethyl ethanoate and water.

questions.stem: CHCl3 + Cl2 → HCl + CCl4. The reaction above is an example of
questions.explanation: A chlorine atom replaces the hydrogen atom in CHCl3: a substitution reaction.

questions.stem: CH3-CH(CH3)-CH=CH-CH3. The IUPAC nomenclature for the compound above is
questions.explanation: The longest chain has five carbons; numbering gives the double bond the lowest number (C-2) and the methyl group is on C-4.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs has compounds that are isomers?
questions.explanation: Propanal and propanone both have the formula C3H6O.

questions.stem: The role of sodium chloride in the preparation of soap is to
options: accelerate the decomposition of the fat or oil
questions.explanation: Adding salt (salting out) makes the soap precipitate, separating it from the glycerol solution.

questions.stem: CH3CH=CH-CHO. The functional group represented in the compound above is
questions.explanation: The -CHO group at the end of the chain is the alkanal (aldehyde) group.

questions.stem: CxHy + 4O2 → 3CO2 + 2H2O. The hydrocarbon CxHy in the reaction above is
questions.explanation: Carbon balance gives x = 3 and hydrogen balance y = 4: C3H4 is propyne (check: 8 O atoms on each side).

questions.stem: An example of a secondary amine is
questions.explanation: Dibutylamine (C4H9)2NH has two alkyl groups on nitrogen; methylamine is primary and trimethylamine tertiary.

questions.stem: The relatively high boiling points of alkanols are due to
questions.explanation: The -OH groups form hydrogen bonds between alkanol molecules.

questions.stem: 35 cm^3 of hydrogen was sparked with 12 cm^3 of oxygen at 110 °C and 760 mm Hg to produce steam. What percentage of the total volume of gas left after the reaction is hydrogen?
questions.explanation: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O(g): 12 cm^3 O2 uses 24 cm^3 H2, leaving 11 cm^3 H2 plus 24 cm^3 steam; 11/35 = 31%.

questions.stem: An element, X, forms a volatile hydride XH3 with a vapour density of 17.0. The relative atomic mass of X is
A mixture of 0.20 mole of Ar, 0.20 mole of N2 and 0.30 mole of He exerts a total pressure of 2.1 atm. The partial pressure of He in the mixture is
questions.explanation: Mole fraction of He = 0.30/0.70; p(He) = (0.30/0.70) x 2.1 = 0.90 atm.

questions.stem: If 30 cm^3 of oxygen diffuses through a porous plug in 7 s, how long will it take 60 cm^3 of chlorine to diffuse through the same plug?
questions.explanation: Time for 60 cm^3 O2 = 14 s; t(Cl2) = 14 x sqrt(71/32) = 20.9 s, about 21 s.

questions.stem: The temperature of a body decreases when drops of liquid placed on it evaporate because
options: the atmospheric vapour pressure has a cooling effect on the body
a temperature gradient exists between the drops of liquid and the body
the heat of vaporization is drawn from the body, causing it to cool
the random motion of the liquid molecules causes a cooling effect on the body
questions.explanation: Evaporating molecules take their latent heat of vaporization from the body, so it cools.

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: The electron configurations of two elements with similar chemical properties are represented by
questions.explanation: Both have one outer s electron (Na and Li), so they are in group I and behave similarly.

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: In the periodic table, what is the property that decreases along the period and increases down the group?
questions.explanation: Atomic radius shrinks across a period (rising nuclear charge) and grows down a group (more shells).

questions.stem: Two elements, P and Q, with atomic numbers 11 and 8 respectively, combine chemically to form PxQy. The values of x and y are
questions.explanation: P is sodium (valency 1) and Q is oxygen (valency 2), giving Na2O: x = 2, y = 1.

Which of the following gases is the most dangerous pollutant?
questions.explanation: CO is colourless and odourless and combines irreversibly with haemoglobin, preventing oxygen transport.

questions.stem: A major process involved in the softening of hard water is the
options: conversion of a soluble calcium salt to its trioxocarbonate(IV)
conversion of an insoluble calcium salt to its trioxocarbonate(IV)
oxidation of calcium atoms to their ions
questions.explanation: Softening (by boiling or washing soda) precipitates dissolved calcium as insoluble CaCO3.

questions.stem: On recrystallization, 20 g of magnesium tetraoxosulphate(VI) forms 41 g of magnesium tetraoxosulphate(VI) crystals, MgSO4.yH2O. The value of y is (Mg = 24, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1)

questions.explanation: An acidic solution (pH 3.0) contains enough H+ to react with Mg and release hydrogen.

questions.stem: Given that 15.00 cm^3 of H2SO4 was required to completely neutralize 25.00 cm^3 of 0.125 mol dm^-3 NaOH, calculate the molar concentration of the acid solution.
questions.explanation: Mol NaOH = 0.003125; H2SO4 needs half = 0.0015625 mol in 0.015 dm^3 = 0.104 mol/dm^3.

questions.stem: When platinum electrodes are used during the electrolysis of copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution, the solution gets progressively
questions.explanation: Cu2+ and OH- are discharged, leaving H+ and SO4^2- in solution, so it becomes increasingly acidic.

questions.stem: One method of driving the position of equilibrium of an endothermic reaction forward is to
options: cool down the apparatus with water
questions.explanation: Raising the temperature favours the endothermic (heat-absorbing) direction.

questions.stem: Oxidation of concentrated hydrochloric acid with manganese(IV) oxide liberates a gas used in the
questions.explanation: The gas is chlorine, which is used to sterilize water.

questions.stem: mE + nF ⇌ pG + qH. In the equation above, the equilibrium constant is given by
questions.explanation: K = products raised to their coefficients divided by reactants raised to theirs.

questions.stem: Coal gas is made up of carbon(II) oxide, hydrogen and
questions.explanation: Coal gas (from destructive distillation of coal) is mainly hydrogen, methane and carbon(II) oxide.

questions.stem: The reaction that occurs during the laboratory test for the presence of tetraoxosulphate(VI) ions is
questions.explanation: Sulphate ions give a white precipitate of BaSO4, insoluble in dilute acid, with barium ions.

questions.stem: The removal of rust from iron by treatment with tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is based on the
questions.explanation: Rust (hydrated iron(III) oxide) is a basic oxide that is neutralized by the acid.

questions.stem: Which of the following additives could improve the quality of steel?
questions.explanation: Chromium and nickel make stainless steel, resistant to corrosion; sulphur and phosphorus are harmful impurities.

questions.stem: Sodium hydroxide is prepared commercially from sodium chloride solution by
options: hydrolysis in steam using a catalyst
treating sodium chloride with ammonia and carbon(IV) oxide
questions.explanation: In the mercury cathode cell, sodium forms an amalgam that reacts with water to give NaOH.

questions.stem: A sample of a substance containing only C and H burns in excess O2 to yield 4.4 g of CO2 and 2.7 g of H2O. The empirical formula of the substance is (C = 12, O = 16, H = 1)
An undesirable paraffin in the petroleum industry which is particularly prone to knocking is
questions.explanation: n-Heptane knocks badly and is assigned octane number 0.

questions.stem: CH3-CH(CH3)-CH(CH2CH3)-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH3. The IUPAC nomenclature of the organic compound with the above structural formula is
questions.explanation: The longest chain has six carbons; numbering for lowest locants gives methyls at 2 and 5 and ethyl at 3.

questions.stem: The reaction of an alkanol with an alkanoic acid in the presence of concentrated H2SO4 will produce an
questions.explanation: Esterification of an alkanol with an alkanoic acid gives an ester (alkanoate).

questions.stem: The final product of the reaction of ethyne with hydrogen iodide is
questions.explanation: Two successive additions of HI (Markovnikov) give 1,1-diiodoethane, CH3CHI2; CH2=CHI is only the intermediate.

questions.stem: Synthetic detergents are preferred to soap for laundry using hard water because
options: detergents are water soluble while soap is not
the calcium salts of detergents are water soluble
the magnesium salt of soap is soluble in hard water
soap does not have a hydrocarbon terminal chain
questions.explanation: Detergents do not form scum because their calcium and magnesium salts are soluble.

questions.stem: The synthetic rubber obtained by the polymerization of chlorobutadiene in the presence of sodium is called
questions.explanation: Polychlorobutadiene (polychloroprene) is neoprene.

questions.stem: 25 cm^3 of 0.02 M KOH neutralized 0.03 g of a monobasic organic acid having the general formula CnH2n+1COOH. The molecular formula of the acid is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)

questions.explanation: CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2 forms a new substance (slaked lime) with evolution of heat, so it is a chemical change.

questions.explanation: By Gay-Lussac's law, 1 volume of propane needs 5 volumes of oxygen: 5 × 50 = 250 cm3.
