questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: Which of the following electron configurations indicates an atom with the highest ionization energy?
questions.explanation: 2,8,7 (chlorine) is a small halogen atom with a nearly full outer shell held close to the nucleus, so it has the highest ionization energy of the four.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: The lines observed in the simple hydrogen spectrum are due to emission of
questions.explanation: Each spectral line is energy (a photon) emitted when an electron drops from a higher to a lower energy level.

questions.stem: The property used in obtaining oxygen and nitrogen industrially from air is the
questions.explanation: Liquefied air is fractionally distilled, separating nitrogen and oxygen by their different boiling points.

questions.stem: Excess phosphorus was burnt in a gas jar and the residual gas passed successively over concentrated KOH solution and concentrated H2SO4 before being collected in a flask. The gases collected are
options: carbon(IV) oxide, nitrogen and the rare gases
nitrogen(IV) oxide and the rare gases
carbon(IV) oxide, nitrogen(IV) oxide and the rare gases
questions.explanation: Phosphorus removes oxygen, KOH absorbs carbon(IV) oxide and conc. H2SO4 removes water vapour, leaving nitrogen and the rare gases.

questions.stem: The soil around a battery manufacturing factory is likely to contain a high concentration of
questions.explanation: Lead-acid batteries use lead and lead compounds, so lead(II) salts contaminate the surrounding soil.

questions.stem: 90.0 g of MgCl2 was placed in 50.0 cm3 of water to give a saturated solution at 298 K. If the solubility of the salt is 8.0 mol dm-3 at the same temperature, what is the mass of the salt left undissolved at the given temperature? [Mg = 24, Cl = 35.5]
questions.explanation: Moles dissolved = 8.0 × 0.050 = 0.40 mol = 0.40 × 95 = 38 g; undissolved = 90 − 38 = 52.0 g.

questions.stem: Soap lather is an example of a colloid in which a
questions.explanation: Lather (foam) consists of air bubbles (gas) dispersed in the soap solution (liquid).

questions.stem: The pH of a solution obtained by mixing 100 cm3 of a 0.1 M HCl solution with 100 cm3 of a 0.2 M solution of NaOH is
What volume of 0.1 mol dm-3 solution of tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid would be needed to dissolve 2.86 g of sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) decahydrate crystals? [H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, S = 32, Na = 23]
questions.explanation: Na2CO3.10H2O = 286 g/mol, so 2.86 g = 0.01 mol; it reacts 1:1 with H2SO4, so V = 0.01/0.1 = 0.1 dm3 = 100 cm3.

questions.stem: 1.2 F of electricity are passed through electrolytic cells containing Na+, Cu2+ and Al3+ in series. How many moles of each metal would be formed at the cathode of each cell?
options: 0.6 mole of Na, 1.2 moles of Cu and 1.2 moles of Al
1.2 moles of Na, 0.6 mole of Cu and 0.4 mole of Al
1.3 moles of Na, 2.4 moles of Cu and 2.4 moles of Al
1.2 moles of Na, 2.4 moles of Cu and 3.6 moles of Al
questions.explanation: Moles deposited = 1.2 F ÷ charge on ion: Na 1.2/1 = 1.2, Cu 1.2/2 = 0.6, Al 1.2/3 = 0.4.

questions.stem: What mass of gold is deposited during the electrolysis of gold(III) tetraoxosulphate(VI) when a current of 15 A is passed for 193 seconds? [Au = 197, F = 96 500 C mol-1]
questions.explanation: Q = 15 × 193 = 2895 C = 0.03 F; Au3+ needs 3 F per mole, so 0.01 mol × 197 = 1.97 g.

questions.stem: Fe(s) + Cu2+(aq) → Fe2+(aq) + Cu(s). From the reaction above it can be inferred that
questions.explanation: Cu2+ gains electrons from Fe and is reduced to Cu, so Cu2+ is the oxidizing agent.

questions.stem: 2FeCl2(s) + Cl2(g) → 2FeCl3(s). The reducing agent in the reaction above is
questions.explanation: Iron in FeCl2 is oxidized from +2 to +3, so FeCl2 donates electrons and is the reducing agent.

questions.stem: The reaction that is accompanied by a decrease in entropy when carried out at constant temperature is
questions.explanation: N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3 reduces 4 moles of gas to 2, so disorder (entropy) decreases; the others increase the number of gas moles.

questions.stem: 32 g of anhydrous copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) dissolved in 1 dm3 of water generated 13.0 kJ of heat. The heat of solution is [CuSO4 = 160]
questions.explanation: 32 g ÷ 160 g/mol = 0.2 mol; 13.0 kJ ÷ 0.2 mol = 65.0 kJ per mole.

questions.stem: Mg2+(aq) + 2e- → Mg(s), E° = −2.370 V; Zn2+(aq) + 2e- → Zn(s), E° = −0.763 V; Cd2+(aq) + 2e- → Cd(s), E° = −0.403 V; Cu2+(aq) + 2e- → Cu(s), E° = +0.403 V. In the electrochemical series above, the strongest reducing agent is
questions.explanation: The metal with the most negative electrode potential (Mg, −2.370 V) loses electrons most readily, so it is the strongest reducing agent.

questions.stem: 2X(g) + Y(g) → Z(g). In the equation above, the rate of formation of Z is found to be independent of the concentration of Y and to quadruple when the concentration of X is doubled. The rate equation for the reaction is
questions.explanation: Zero order in Y gives [Y]^0; doubling [X] quadruples the rate, so it is second order in X: R = k[X]^2[Y]^0.

questions.stem: 2Cl2(g) + 2H2O(g) ⇌ 4HCl(g) + O2(g), ΔH = +115 kJ mol-1. In the above equilibrium reaction, a decrease in temperature will
options: have no effect on the equilibrium state
double the rate of the reverse reaction
questions.explanation: The forward reaction is endothermic, so lowering the temperature shifts the equilibrium to the exothermic (reverse) direction.

questions.stem: 3CuO(s) + 2NH3(g) → 3Cu(s) + 3H2O(l) + N2(g); 2NH3(g) + 3Cl2(g) → 6HCl(g) + N2(g). The reactions represented by the equations above demonstrate the
questions.explanation: In both reactions ammonia is oxidized to nitrogen while reducing CuO to Cu and Cl2 to HCl, showing its reducing property.

questions.stem: A gas that turns a filter paper previously soaked in lead ethanoate solution black is
questions.explanation: H2S reacts with lead ethanoate to form black lead(II) sulphide.

questions.stem: A solution containing chloride gives a white precipitate with silver trioxonitrate(V) solution. The precipitate will be insoluble in dilute
options: HNO3 but soluble in ammonia solution
HCl but soluble in ammonia solution
questions.explanation: AgCl does not dissolve in dilute HNO3 but dissolves in ammonia solution as the complex [Ag(NH3)2]+.

questions.stem: The oxide that remains unchanged when heated in hydrogen is
questions.explanation: Zinc is high in the reactivity series, so hydrogen cannot reduce ZnO, while CuO, Fe2O3 and PbO2 are reduced.

questions.stem: A common characteristic shared by iron and aluminium is that both
questions.explanation: Iron is extracted by reduction with carbon and aluminium by electrolytic (cathodic) reduction; Al2O3 is amphoteric, Al shows only +3, and both hydroxides are insoluble.

questions.stem: Alloys are often used in preference to pure metals because
options: metallic properties are improved in alloys
alloys are a mixture of metals
questions.explanation: Alloying improves properties such as hardness, strength and corrosion resistance compared with the pure metals.

questions.stem: CH3CH2CH(OH)CH(CH3)2. The IUPAC nomenclature for the above compound is
questions.explanation: The longest chain has 5 carbons; numbering gives the OH on C3 and the methyl on C2: 2-methylpentan-3-ol.

questions.stem: nCH2=CH2 → (O2 initiator) → (−CH2−CH2−)n. The above equation represents the manufacture of
questions.explanation: Addition polymerization of ethene gives polyethene (polythene).

questions.stem: One mole of a hydrocarbon contains 6 g of hydrogen. If the molecular weight is 54, the hydrocarbon is an
questions.explanation: 6 g H = 6 H atoms; (54 − 6)/12 = 4 C, so the formula is C4H6, which fits CnH2n−2 (an alkyne).

questions.stem: The products obtained when a pure hydrocarbon is burnt in excess oxygen are
questions.explanation: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon in excess oxygen gives carbon(IV) oxide and water.

questions.stem: How many structural isomers can be drawn for the non-cyclic alkanol with molecular formula C4H10O?
questions.explanation: There are four: butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

questions.stem: An example of an aromatic compound is
questions.explanation: C6H5OH (phenol) contains a benzene ring, so it is aromatic; the others are aliphatic.

questions.stem: Terylene is synthesized from ethane-1,2-diol and benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid by
questions.explanation: The diol and diacid link up through ester bonds, losing water each time, so this is condensation polymerization.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true concerning the properties of benzene and hexane?
questions.explanation: Hexane undergoes substitution with halogens in light and benzene typically undergoes substitution, so substitution is common to both.

questions.stem: 200 cm3 each of 0.1 M solutions of lead(II) trioxonitrate(V) and hydrochloric acid were mixed. Assuming that lead(II) chloride is completely insoluble, calculate the mass of lead(II) chloride that will be precipitated. [Pb = 207, Cl = 35.5, N = 14, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Each reagent is 0.02 mol; Pb2+ + 2Cl- → PbCl2, so Cl- limits: 0.01 mol PbCl2 × 278 g/mol = 2.78 g.

questions.stem: 56.00 cm3 of a gas at s.t.p. weighed 0.11 g. What is the vapour density of the gas? [Molar volume of a gas at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm3]
questions.explanation: Molar mass = 0.11 g ÷ (56/22 400) mol = 44 g/mol; vapour density = 44/2 = 22.

questions.stem: Which of the following gases will diffuse fastest when passed through a porous plug? [H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16]
questions.explanation: By Graham's law the lightest gas diffuses fastest; methane (16) is lighter than ammonia (17), oxygen (32) and propane (44).

questions.stem: Which of the following will have its mass increased when heated in air?
questions.explanation: Magnesium combines with oxygen to form magnesium oxide, so its mass increases; copper pyrites loses sulphur as SO2.

questions.stem: What is the temperature of a given mass of a gas initially at 0 °C and 9 atm, if the pressure is reduced to 3 atmospheres at constant volume?
questions.explanation: At constant volume P/T is constant: T2 = 273 × 3/9 = 91 K.

questions.stem: Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl2(aq) + H2(g). From the equation above, the mass of magnesium required to react with 250 cm3 of 0.5 M HCl is [Mg = 24]
In which of the following are water molecules in the most disorderly arrangement?
questions.explanation: Gas molecules are the most disordered, so steam has the highest disorder.

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: In order to remove one electron from the 3s-orbital of a gaseous sodium atom, about 496 kJ mol-1 of energy is required. This energy is referred to as
questions.explanation: The energy needed to remove an electron from a gaseous atom is the (first) ionization energy.

questions.stem: Nitrogen obtained from the liquefaction of air has a higher density than that obtained from nitrogen-containing compounds because the former contains
questions.explanation: Atmospheric nitrogen contains denser rare gases (mainly argon), making it denser than chemically prepared nitrogen.

questions.stem: The method that can be used to convert hard water to soft water is
options: the use of an ion exchange resin
questions.explanation: An ion exchange resin replaces Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions with Na+ ions, softening the water.

questions.topic: Metals of the first transition series
questions.stem: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d7 4s2. An element with the electron configuration above is a
questions.explanation: The partly filled 3d sub-level (3d7, cobalt) marks it as a transition element.

questions.stem: Given that electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group in the periodic table, in which of the following compounds will the molecules be held together by the strongest hydrogen bond?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element, so H–F molecules form the strongest hydrogen bonds.

questions.stem: 0.25 mole of hydrogen chloride was dissolved in distilled water and the volume made up to 0.50 dm3. If 15.00 cm3 of the solution requires 12.50 cm3 of aqueous sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) for neutralization, calculate the concentration of the alkaline solution.
The correct order of increasing oxidation number of the transition metal ions for the compounds K2Cr2O7, V2O5 and KMnO4 is
questions.explanation: Oxidation numbers: V in V2O5 = +5, Cr in K2Cr2O7 = +6, Mn in KMnO4 = +7.

questions.stem: The set of pollutants that is most likely to be produced when petrol is accidentally spilled on plastic materials and ignited is
questions.explanation: Burning hydrocarbons give CO and CO2, while chlorinated plastics such as PVC release HCl.

questions.stem: What is observed when aqueous solutions of each of tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid, potassium trioxoiodate(V) and potassium iodide are mixed together?
questions.explanation: In acid, IO3- oxidizes I- to iodine (IO3- + 5I- + 6H+ → 3I2 + 3H2O), which colours the solution reddish-brown.

questions.stem: The entropy and enthalpy of a system are a measure of
options: degree of disorderliness and heat content respectively
heat content and degree of disorderliness respectively
heat content of a system only
questions.explanation: Entropy measures disorder and enthalpy measures heat content.

questions.stem: 2SO2(g) + O2(g) → 2SO3(g). In the chemical reaction above, the substance that will increase the rate of production of sulphur(VI) oxide is
questions.explanation: Vanadium(V) oxide is the catalyst used in the Contact process.

questions.stem: N2O4(g) ⇌ 2NO2(g). An increase in total pressure of the equilibrium reaction above will
options: produce more of NO2(g) in the mixture
convert all of N2O4(g) to NO2(g)
have no effect on the concentrations of N2O4(g) and NO2(g)
produce more of N2O4(g) in the mixture
questions.explanation: Higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules (1 mol N2O4 against 2 mol NO2), so more N2O4 forms.

questions.stem: What quantity of electricity will liberate 0.125 mole of oxygen molecules during the electrolysis of dilute sodium chloride solution? [F = 96 500 C mol-1]
X + Y → Z. The rate equation for the chemical reaction above is −d[X]/dt = k[X]^2[Y]. The overall order of the reaction is
questions.explanation: Overall order = sum of exponents = 2 + 1 = 3.

questions.stem: When a current I was passed through an electrolyte solution for 40 minutes, a mass x g of a univalent metal was deposited at the cathode. What mass of the metal will be deposited when a current 2I is passed through the solution for 10 minutes?
questions.explanation: Mass is proportional to charge It: (2I × 10)/(I × 40) = 1/2, so the mass is x/2 g.

questions.stem: RS(aq) + HF(aq) → RF(s) + HS(aq), ΔH = −65.7 kJ mol-1. From the equation above, it can be deduced that
options: the heat content of the reactants is lower than that of the products
the heat content of the reactants is higher than that of the products
a large amount of heat is absorbed
questions.explanation: A negative ΔH (exothermic) means the reactants have a higher heat content than the products.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true of the electrochemical series?
options: Electropositivity of metals increases down the series
Electropositivity of non-metals decreases down the series
Electronegativity of non-metals increases down the series
Electropositivity of metals decreases down the series
questions.explanation: The series starts with the most electropositive metals (K, Na, Ca), so the electropositivity of metals decreases down the series.

questions.stem: The gas that will form a white precipitate with acidified silver trioxonitrate(V) is
questions.explanation: HCl gives Cl- ions, which form a white precipitate of AgCl.

questions.stem: Chlorine, bromine and iodine resemble one another in that they
options: react violently with hydrogen without heating
displace one another from solutions of their salts
questions.explanation: All three halogens react with (dissolve in) alkalis; only bromine is a liquid and iodine cannot displace the others.

questions.stem: A pair of compounds that can be used to generate a gas which has a physiological effect on human beings is
questions.explanation: Heating NaNO3 with NH4Cl forms ammonium trioxonitrate(V), which decomposes to dinitrogen(I) oxide (laughing gas), a gas with a physiological effect.

questions.stem: Hydrogen is used in oxy-hydrogen flames for melting metals because it
options: evolves a lot of heat when burnt
questions.explanation: Hydrogen burns in oxygen with a very hot flame because a lot of heat is released.

questions.stem: What properties of duralumin make it more useful than its constituent metals?
options: It is heavy with a high melting point
It is malleable and has high density
questions.explanation: Duralumin (Al with Cu, Mg, Mn) is strong yet light, so it is used in aircraft bodies.

questions.stem: The pair of metals in the reactivity series that are usually extracted by the electrolysis of their ores is
questions.explanation: Very reactive metals such as magnesium and calcium are extracted by electrolysis of their fused ores.

questions.stem: A metal that can be extracted from cassiterite is
questions.explanation: Cassiterite (SnO2) is the chief ore of tin.

questions.stem: Which of the following metals is passive to concentrated trioxonitrate(V) acid?
questions.explanation: Concentrated HNO3 forms a protective oxide layer on iron, making it passive.

questions.stem: 2-methylprop-1-ene is an isomer of
questions.explanation: 2-methylprop-1-ene and but-2-ene are both C4H8; the other options are C5H10.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a solvent for perfumes?
questions.explanation: Ethanol (C2H5OH) is the usual solvent for perfumes and cosmetics.

questions.stem: When excess ethanol is heated to 145 °C in the presence of concentrated H2SO4, the product is
questions.explanation: With excess ethanol at about 140–145 °C, concentrated H2SO4 dehydrates two ethanol molecules to diethyl ether.

questions.stem: How many grammes of bromine will saturate 5.2 g of but-1-ene-3-yne? [C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80]
questions.explanation: C4H4 = 52 g/mol, so 5.2 g = 0.1 mol; one C=C and one C≡C take 3 mol Br2 per mole: 0.3 × 160 = 48.0 g.

questions.stem: Polyvinyl chloride is used to produce
questions.explanation: PVC is a tough plastic widely used to make pipes.

questions.stem: When the two end alkyl groups of ethyl ethanoate are interchanged, the compound formed is known as
questions.explanation: CH3COOC2H5 with the alkyl groups swapped becomes C2H5COOCH3, methyl propanoate.

questions.stem: Sieving is a technique used to separate mixtures containing solid particles of
questions.explanation: A sieve separates solid particles according to differences in their sizes.

questions.stem: Which of the compounds is composed of Al, Si, O and H?
questions.explanation: Clay is a hydrated aluminium silicate, containing Al, Si, O and H.

questions.stem: 50 cm3 of carbon(II) oxide was exploded with 150 cm3 of air containing 20% oxygen by volume. Which of the reactants was in excess?
questions.explanation: The air holds 30 cm3 of O2; 2CO + O2 → 2CO2 means 50 cm3 CO needs only 25 cm3 O2, so oxygen is in excess.

questions.stem: How many moles of HCl will be required to react with potassium heptaoxodichromate(VI) to produce 3 moles of chlorine?
questions.explanation: K2Cr2O7 + 14HCl → 2KCl + 2CrCl3 + 7H2O + 3Cl2, so 14 mol HCl give 3 mol Cl2.

questions.stem: The ratio of the initial to the final pressure of a given mass of gas is 1:1.5. Calculate the final volume of the gas if the initial volume was 300 cm3 at the same temperature.
The partial pressure of oxygen in a sample of air is 452 mmHg and the total pressure is 780 mmHg. What is the mole fraction of oxygen?
questions.explanation: Mole fraction = partial pressure ÷ total pressure = 452/780 = 0.579.

questions.stem: The fundamental difference between the three states of matter is the
options: number of particles in each state
shape of the container they occupy
degree of movement of their particles
questions.explanation: Solids, liquids and gases differ in how freely their particles move, which depends on the forces between them.

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct about the periodic table?
options: Elements in the same period have the same number of valence electrons
The valence electrons of the elements in the same period increase progressively across the period
Elements in the same group have the same number of electron shells
The non-metallic properties of the elements tend to decrease across each period
questions.explanation: Across a period, each element has one more valence electron than the one before it.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of bonding does not involve the formation of a new substance?
questions.explanation: Metallic bonding holds atoms of the same metal together without forming a new compound.

questions.stem: The shapes of CO2, H2O and CH4 respectively are
questions.explanation: CO2 is linear (two bond pairs), H2O is bent (two lone pairs) and CH4 is tetrahedral.

questions.topic: Air as a mixture and uses of noble gases
questions.stem: The noble gas, argon, is used for
questions.explanation: Argon provides an inert shielding atmosphere in electric arc welding.

questions.stem: A side effect of soft water is that
options: it attacks lead contained in pipes
it encourages the growth of bacteria
questions.explanation: Soft water dissolves lead from lead pipes (plumbosolvency), which can cause lead poisoning.

questions.topic: Metals of the first transition series
questions.stem: Water molecules can be ligands especially when they are bonded to
questions.explanation: Transition metal ions have vacant d-orbitals that accept lone pairs from water to form complex (aqua) ions.

questions.stem: The air pollutant unknown in nature is
questions.explanation: DDT is a synthetic insecticide that does not occur naturally; the others are formed naturally too.

questions.stem: 10 dm3 of distilled water was used to wash 2.0 g of a precipitate of AgCl. If the solubility product of AgCl is 2.0 × 10^-10 mol2 dm-6, what quantity of silver was lost in the process?
questions.explanation: Solubility s = sqrt(Ksp) = sqrt(2.0 × 10^-10) = 1.414 × 10^-5 mol dm-3 of dissolved silver.

questions.stem: Hydration of ions in solution is associated with
questions.explanation: Attraction between ions and water molecules releases energy, so hydration is exothermic.

questions.stem: HCl(aq) + H2O(l) → H3O+(aq) + Cl-(aq). In the reaction above, Cl-(aq) is the
questions.explanation: HCl donates a proton to become Cl-, so Cl- is the conjugate base of HCl.

questions.stem: The pOH of a solution of 0.25 mol dm-3 of hydrochloric acid is
MnO4-(aq) + 8H+(aq) + Y → Mn2+(aq) + 4H2O(l). Y in the equation above represents
questions.explanation: Mn changes from +7 to +2, a gain of 5 electrons (charge also balances: −1 + 8 − 5 = +2).

questions.stem: ½Zn2+(aq) + e- → ½Zn(s). In the reaction above, calculate the quantity of electricity required to discharge zinc. [F = 96 500 C mol-1]
questions.explanation: The equation involves 1 mole of electrons, i.e. 1 F = 96 500 C = 9.650 × 10^4 C.

questions.stem: Given that M is the mass of substance deposited in an electrolysis and Q the quantity of electricity consumed, then Faraday's law can be written as
questions.explanation: Faraday's first law: mass deposited is proportional to the charge passed, M = ZQ, where Z is the electrochemical equivalent.

questions.stem: 0.46 g of ethanol when burned raised the temperature of 50 g of water by 14.3 K. Calculate the heat of combustion of ethanol. [C = 12, O = 16, H = 1; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g-1 K-1]
questions.explanation: Heat = 50 × 4.2 × 14.3 = 3003 J ≈ 3.0 kJ for 0.46/46 = 0.01 mol, so ΔH = −300 kJ mol-1 (exothermic).

questions.stem: Powdered marble reacts faster with hydrochloric acid solution than the granular form because the powdered form has
questions.explanation: Powdering exposes a larger surface area, so collisions with the acid happen more often.

questions.stem: For a reaction in equilibrium, the species involved in the equilibrium constant expression are
questions.explanation: Pure solids and liquids have constant concentrations and are left out; only gases and dissolved species appear.

questions.stem: A phenomenon where an element exists in different forms in the same physical state is known as
questions.explanation: Allotropy is the existence of an element in two or more forms in the same physical state (e.g. diamond and graphite).

questions.stem: The substance often used for vulcanization of rubber is
questions.explanation: Vulcanization cross-links rubber chains with sulphur, making the rubber harder and more elastic.

questions.stem: The refreshing and characteristic taste of soda water and other soft drinks is as a result of the presence in them of
questions.explanation: Soft drinks are carbonated: dissolved CO2 gives the fizz and the sharp taste.

questions.stem: A form of carbon used for absorbing poisonous gases and purification of noble gases is
questions.explanation: Wood charcoal has a high adsorptive surface and is used in gas masks and to purify noble gases; animal charcoal is used to decolourize sugar.

questions.stem: Synthesis gas is a mixture of
questions.explanation: Synthesis gas (syngas) is carbon(II) oxide and hydrogen.

questions.stem: Potassium vapour burns with a
questions.explanation: Potassium gives a lilac (violet) flame colour.

questions.stem: A common characteristic of copper and silver in their usage as coinage metals is that they
questions.explanation: Copper and silver are low in the reactivity series, so they resist oxidation (corrosion), which suits coins.

questions.stem: Haematite is an ore of
questions.explanation: Haematite (Fe2O3) is the main ore of iron.

questions.stem: The least easily oxidized of the metals below is
questions.explanation: Zinc is the lowest of the four in the reactivity series, so it is the least easily oxidized.

questions.stem: The repeating unit in natural rubber is
questions.explanation: Natural rubber is poly(isoprene), i.e. poly(2-methylbuta-1,3-diene).

questions.stem: The conditions necessary for the extraction of a water molecule from two molecules of ethanol are
options: less acid and a lower temperature
excess acid and a lower temperature
excess acid and a higher temperature
less acid and a higher temperature
questions.explanation: Diethyl ether forms with excess ethanol (less acid) at about 140 °C; excess acid at about 170 °C gives ethene instead.

questions.stem: The chlorinated alkane often used industrially to remove grease is
questions.explanation: Tetrachloromethane (CCl4) is a non-flammable solvent long used for degreasing and dry cleaning.

questions.stem: CH3−CH2−CO−OCH2CH3. The compound above is an
questions.explanation: It contains the −COO− linkage (ethyl propanoate), so it is an ester.

questions.stem: Alkanones are generally obtained by the oxidation of
questions.explanation: Oxidizing a secondary alkanol gives an alkanone; primary alkanols give alkanals.

questions.stem: Sucrose is made up of
questions.explanation: Sucrose is a disaccharide of glucose and fructose.

questions.stem: 25 cm3 of a gas X contains Z molecules at 15 °C and 75 mmHg. How many molecules will 25 cm3 of another gas Y contain at the same temperature and pressure?
questions.explanation: Avogadro's law: equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules, so Z.

questions.stem: What mass of water is produced when 8.0 g of hydrogen reacts with excess oxygen?
questions.explanation: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O: 8.0 g H2 = 4 mol, giving 4 mol H2O = 4 × 18 = 72.0 g.

questions.topic: Periodic table and periodicity of elements
questions.stem: Four elements W, X, Y and Z have atomic numbers 2, 6, 16 and 20 respectively. Which of these elements is a metal?
questions.explanation: Atomic number 20 is calcium (2,8,8,2), a metal; 2 is helium, 6 is carbon and 16 is sulphur.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: An element X with relative atomic mass 16.2 contains two isotopes, 16/8 X with relative abundance of 90% and m/8 X with relative abundance of 10%. The value of m is
Cancerous growths are cured by exposure to
questions.explanation: Gamma rays (e.g. from cobalt-60) are used in radiotherapy to destroy cancer cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct about the average kinetic energy of the molecules of a gas?
options: It increases with increase in pressure
It increases with increase in temperature
It increases with increase in volume
questions.explanation: Average kinetic energy of gas molecules is proportional to the absolute temperature.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: Millikan's contribution to the development of atomic theory is the determination of
questions.explanation: Millikan's oil-drop experiment measured the charge on the electron.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: A particle that contains 9 protons, 10 neutrons and 10 electrons is
options: a neutral atom of a metal
a neutral atom of a non-metal
questions.explanation: It has one more electron than protons, so it carries a −1 charge (the fluoride ion).

questions.stem: An oxide XO2 has a vapour density of 32. What is the atomic mass of X?
questions.explanation: Relative molecular mass = 2 × 32 = 64; X = 64 − 32 = 32.

questions.stem: The chemical used for coagulation in water purification is
questions.explanation: Alum/aluminium sulphate coagulates suspended particles so they settle out.

questions.stem: Phosphorus is stored under water to prevent it from
questions.explanation: White phosphorus ignites spontaneously in air, so it is kept under water.

questions.stem: Pure solvents are obtained by
questions.explanation: Distillation boils off the solvent and condenses it, leaving the solute behind.

questions.stem: Deliquescent substances are used for
questions.explanation: Deliquescent substances (e.g. CaCl2) absorb moisture strongly, so they are used as drying agents.

questions.stem: What is the decrease in volume of air when pyrogallol is shaken with 30.00 cm3 of air?
questions.explanation: Alkaline pyrogallol absorbs the oxygen, about 21% of air: 0.21 × 30.00 = 6.30 cm3.

questions.stem: The pollution from petroleum spillage in rivers and lakes can best be dispersed by
options: passing of ships through the area
questions.explanation: Detergents emulsify the oil into tiny droplets that disperse in the water.

questions.explanation: Copper is oxidized from 0 to +2, donating electrons, so it acts as the reducing agent.

questions.stem: NH3(g) + HCl(g) → NH4Cl(s). The entropy change in the system above is
questions.explanation: Two gases combine into a solid, so disorder decreases and ΔS is negative.

both carbon and sulphur contribute 89 kJ of energy

questions.stem: P(g) + Q(g) ⇌ 3R(s) + S(g). Which of the following will increase the yield of R?
questions.explanation: Removing the product S shifts the equilibrium to the right, producing more R; a catalyst does not change the yield.

questions.stem: Ethanoic acid is
questions.explanation: CH3COOH has only one ionizable hydrogen, so it is monobasic.

questions.stem: A metal M displaces zinc from zinc chloride solution. This shows that
options: M is more electronegative than zinc
zinc is above hydrogen in the series
electrons flow from zinc to M
M is more electropositive than zinc
questions.explanation: A metal displaces another from its salt solution only if it is higher (more electropositive) in the series.

questions.stem: In which of the following reactions does reduction take place?
questions.explanation: Reduction is gain of electrons: 2H+ gain two electrons to form H2; the others are electron losses.

questions.stem: When ΔH is negative, a reaction is said to be
questions.explanation: A negative enthalpy change means heat is given out: an exothermic reaction.

questions.stem: Proteins in acid solution undergo
questions.explanation: Acids hydrolyse the peptide bonds of proteins to give amino acids.

questions.stem: Fermentation is the
options: breaking down of carbohydrate to glucose
breaking down of sugar to carbohydrate
conversion of sugar to alcohol in the presence of yeast
conversion of alcohol to sugar in the presence of yeast
questions.explanation: Zymase in yeast converts sugar (glucose) into ethanol and carbon(IV) oxide.

questions.stem: Catalytic hydrogenation of benzene produces
questions.explanation: Benzene adds three molecules of H2 over a nickel catalyst to give cyclohexane, C6H12.

questions.stem: A characteristic reaction of the compounds with the general formula CnH2n is
questions.explanation: CnH2n is the alkene series; alkenes undergo addition reactions, including addition polymerization.

questions.stem: When chlorine is passed into water and the resulting solution exposed to sunlight, the products formed are
questions.explanation: Chlorine water forms HOCl, which decomposes in sunlight: 2HOCl → 2HCl + O2.

questions.stem: The pair of organic compounds that are isomers is
questions.explanation: But-1-ene and but-2-ene share the formula C4H8 but differ in the position of the double bond.

questions.explanation: Concentrated H2SO4 removes the elements of water from sugar, leaving carbon: it is a dehydrating agent.

questions.stem: During the vulcanization of rubber, sulphur is added to
questions.explanation: Sulphur forms cross-links (bridges) between rubber chains.

questions.stem: When sodium reacts with water, the resulting solution is
questions.explanation: 2Na + 2H2O → 2NaOH + H2, and NaOH is a strong alkali.

questions.stem: The general formula for the alkanals is
questions.explanation: Alkanals (aldehydes) contain the −CHO group: RCHO.

questions.stem: Which of the following metals burns with a brick-red flame?
questions.explanation: Calcium gives a brick-red flame; sodium gives golden-yellow and magnesium a brilliant white light.

questions.stem: A trihydric alkanol is
questions.explanation: Glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) has three −OH groups.

questions.stem: The main impurity in iron ore during the extraction of iron is
questions.explanation: Silica (SiO2) is the main impurity; limestone removes it as calcium trioxosilicate(IV) slag.

questions.stem: The formula CH2O for ethanoic acid is regarded as its
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid is C2H4O2; CH2O is its simplest whole-number ratio, i.e. the empirical formula.

questions.stem: Which of the following gases contains the least number of atoms at s.t.p?
questions.explanation: Moles of atoms: Ar 7 x 1 = 7, Cl2 4 x 2 = 8, O3 3 x 3 = 9, C4H10 1 x 14 = 14; argon has the fewest.

questions.stem: The chromatographic separation of ink is based on the ability of the components to
options: dissolve in each other in the column
move at different speeds in the column
questions.explanation: Components are separated because they are adsorbed to different extents and so move at different speeds through the medium.

questions.stem: A compound contain 31.91% potassium, 28.93% chlorine and the rest oxygen. What is the chemical formula of the compound?
The gas that gives brown colouration in brown ring test is
questions.explanation: In the brown ring test the nitrate is reduced to NO, which combines with FeSO4 to form the brown FeSO4.NO complex.

questions.stem: Which of the following gives a precipitate when treated with NaOH solution?
questions.explanation: Al3+ ions react with NaOH to give a white gelatinous precipitate of Al(OH)3; the others give no precipitate.

questions.stem: The reaction of an alkene with hydrogen in the presence of a catalyst is
questions.explanation: Hydrogen adds across the C=C double bond (hydrogenation), which is an addition reaction.

questions.stem: A rock sample was added to cold dilute HNO3. The gas evolved was passed into a solution of acidified K2Cr2O7 and the solution turned green. The rock sample contains
questions.explanation: Acid liberates SO2 from a sulphite; SO2 reduces orange dichromate(VI) to green chromium(III).

questions.stem: The intermediate product formed when ethanol is progressively oxidized to ethanoic acid with potassium heptaoxodichromate (VI) is
questions.explanation: Ethanol is oxidised first to ethanal (CH3CHO) and then to ethanoic acid.

questions.stem: CH3CH2CH(OH)CH3. The compound above is a
questions.explanation: The carbon bearing the OH group is attached to two other carbon atoms, so butan-2-ol is a secondary alkanol.

questions.stem: The most important use of hydrogen is in the
questions.explanation: Most industrial hydrogen is consumed in the Haber process for making ammonia.

questions.stem: Which of the following polymers is suitable for packaging and electrical insulation?
questions.explanation: Polyethene is flexible, cheap, water-resistant and a good insulator, so it is used for packaging films and cable insulation.

questions.stem: The boiling of fat and aqueous caustic soda is referred to as
questions.explanation: Alkaline hydrolysis of fats with NaOH gives soap and glycerol; this is saponification.

questions.stem: Ordinary glass is manufactured from silica, CaCO3 and
questions.explanation: Soda-lime glass is made by fusing sand (silica), limestone and sodium carbonate (soda ash).

questions.stem: The number of isomers formed by C6H14 is
questions.explanation: Hexane has five structural isomers: hexane, 2-methylpentane, 3-methylpentane, 2,2-dimethylbutane and 2,3-dimethylbutane.

questions.stem: Which of these pairs are synthetic and natural macromolecules respectively?
options: Nylon and polyethylene, creatine and haemoglobin
Nylon and creatine, polyethylene and haemoglobin
Polyethylene and creatine, nylon and haemoglobin
Haemoglobin and nylon, creatine and polyethylene
questions.explanation: Nylon and polyethylene are man-made polymers; creatine and haemoglobin occur naturally in living things.

questions.stem: An example of an element that can catenate is
questions.explanation: Carbon readily forms long chains and rings of its own atoms (catenation).

questions.stem: Ethanol can easily be produced by
questions.explanation: Starch is hydrolysed to sugars which yeast ferments to ethanol.

questions.stem: Hydrogen is readily released when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with
questions.explanation: Only sodium is above hydrogen in the activity series; Ag, Au and Cu do not displace hydrogen from dilute acid.

questions.stem: A gas X diffuses twice as fast as gas Y under the same condition. If the relative molecular mass of X is 28, calculate the relative molecular mass of Y
questions.explanation: Graham's law: rX/rY = sqrt(MY/MX) = 2, so MY = 4 x 28 = 112.

questions.stem: Which of the following chlorides would exhibit the least ionic character?
questions.explanation: Al3+ is small and highly charged, so it strongly polarises chloride ions; AlCl3 is largely covalent.

questions.stem: A fixed mass of gas has a volume of 92 cm3 at 3 °C. What will be its volume at 18 °C if the pressure remains constant?
questions.explanation: Charles' law: V2 = 92 x 291/276 = 97.0 cm3.

questions.stem: The processes which return carbon(IV) oxide to the atmosphere include
questions.explanation: Respiration, decay and combustion all release CO2; photosynthesis removes it.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: The postulate of Dalton's atomic theory which still holds is that
options: all elements are made of small indivisible particles
particles of different elements combine in a simple whole number ratio
atoms can neither be created nor destroyed
the particles of the same element are exactly alike
questions.explanation: Atoms are divisible, isotopes differ in mass and nuclear reactions change atoms, but combination in simple whole-number ratios still holds.

questions.stem: If 0.75 mole of cyclopropane and 0.66 mole of oxygen are mixed in a vessel with a total pressure of 0.7 atmosphere, what is the partial pressure of oxygen in the mixture?

questions.stem: When H2S is passed into a solution of iron (III) chloride, the solution turns
questions.explanation: H2S reduces Fe3+ (yellow-brown) to Fe2+ (pale green), itself being oxidised to sulphur.

questions.stem: Which of the following equations shows that a reaction is in equilibrium?
questions.explanation: At equilibrium there is no net driving force, so the free energy change ΔG is zero.

questions.stem: Cu2S(s) + O2(g) → 2Cu(s) + SO2(g). What is the change in the oxidation number of copper in the reaction above?
questions.explanation: In Cu2S copper is +1 (sulphur is -2); as the free metal it is 0.

questions.stem: In the reaction E + F ⇌ G + H, the backward reaction is favoured if the concentration of
questions.explanation: Removing a reactant (E) shifts the equilibrium to the left, by Le Chatelier's principle.

questions.stem: The products of the electrolysis of dilute sodium hydroxide using platinum electrodes are
questions.explanation: OH- is discharged at the anode to give O2 and H+ (from water) at the cathode to give H2; in effect water is electrolysed.

questions.stem: PCl5(g) ⇌ PCl3(g) + Cl2(g). In the reaction above, a decrease in pressure will
questions.explanation: Lower pressure favours the side with more gas molecules (2 on the right), so more PCl3 forms.

questions.stem: The Arrhenius equation expresses the relationship between the speed of a reaction and its
questions.explanation: k = A e^(-Ea/RT) relates the rate constant to the activation energy (and temperature).

questions.stem: What amount of mercury would be liberated if the same quantity of electricity that liberated 0.65 g of zinc is supplied? [Zn = 65, Hg = 201]
questions.explanation: 0.65 g Zn = 0.01 mol Zn2+ = 0.02 F; this deposits 0.01 mol Hg2+ = 0.01 x 201 = 2.01 g.

questions.stem: When dissolved in water, NaOH flakes show
questions.explanation: Dissolving NaOH releases heat; the solution becomes warm.

questions.stem: Steam changes the colour of anhydrous cobalt (II) chloride from
questions.explanation: Anhydrous CoCl2 is blue and turns pink on hydration; it is a test for water.

questions.stem: Which of the following solutions containing only hydroxyl ions will liberate hydrogen gas when reacted with magnesium metal?
questions.explanation: [OH-] = 10^-12 gives pOH 12, pH 2: the solution is acidic, and acids react with Mg to give H2.

questions.stem: The solubility of a salt of molar mass 101 g at 20 °C is 0.34 mol dm^-3. If 3.40 g of the salt is dissolved completely in 250 cm3 of water in beaker, the resulting solution is
questions.explanation: 3.40/101 = 0.0337 mol in 0.25 dm3 = 0.135 mol dm^-3, less than 0.34 mol dm^-3, so it is unsaturated.

questions.stem: 25 cm3 of a 0.2 mol dm^-3 solution of Na2CO3 requires 20 cm3 of a solution of HCl for neutralization. The concentration of the HCl solution is
When a salt loses its water of crystallization to the atmosphere on exposure, the process is said to be
questions.explanation: Efflorescent salts (e.g. Na2CO3.10H2O) lose water of crystallisation to the air.

questions.stem: Three drops of 1.0 mol dm^-3 solution of NaOH are added to 20 cm3 of a solution of pH 8.4. The pH of the resulting solution will be
options: close to that of pure water.
questions.explanation: Adding strong alkali increases [OH-], so the pH rises above 8.4.

questions.stem: Tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid burns the skin by
questions.explanation: Concentrated H2SO4 is a powerful dehydrating agent and removes water from skin tissue.

questions.stem: The substance least considered as a source of environmental pollution is
questions.explanation: Silicate minerals are inert natural rock materials; the others are radioactive or toxic pollutants.

questions.stem: The property which makes alcohol soluble in water is the
questions.explanation: The -OH group of the alcohol forms hydrogen bonds with water molecules.

questions.stem: The furring of kettles is caused by the presence in water of
questions.explanation: On boiling, dissolved Ca(HCO3)2 (temporary hardness) decomposes to insoluble CaCO3, which deposits as fur.

questions.stem: What volume of oxygen is produced from the decomposition of 2 moles of KClO3 at s.t.p? [Molar volume of a gas at s.t.p = 22.4 dm3]
questions.explanation: 2KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2: 2 mol KClO3 give 3 mol O2 = 3 x 22.4 = 67.2 dm3.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a physical change?
questions.explanation: Freezing is only a change of state and is reversible; the others form new substances.

questions.stem: What is the percentage by mass of oxygen in Al2(SO4)3.2H2O? [Al = 27, S = 32, H = 1, O = 16]
The filter in a cigarette reduces the nicotine content by
questions.explanation: Nicotine and tar particles are held on the surface of the filter material, i.e. adsorbed.

questions.explanation: Balancing H: p = 2 x 4 = 8; balancing N: 8 = 6 + x, so x = 2.

questions.topic: Air as a mixture and uses of noble gases
questions.stem: The noble gases owe their inactivity to
questions.explanation: Their outer shells are completely filled (octet, or duplet for helium), so they neither gain, lose nor share electrons readily.

questions.stem: According to the kinetic theory, an increase in temperature causes the kinetic energy of particles to
questions.explanation: Average kinetic energy of particles is proportional to absolute temperature.

questions.stem: A gas exerts pressure on its container because
options: some of its molecules are moving faster than others
of the collision of the molecules with each other
of the mass of the molecules of gas
the molecules of a gas collide with walls of the container.
questions.explanation: Gas pressure results from the force of molecules colliding with the walls of the container.

questions.topic: Atoms, molecules and ions; atomic structure
questions.stem: When cathode rays are deflected onto the electrode of an electrometer, the instrument becomes
questions.explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons, which carry negative charge.

questions.stem: The weakest attractive forces that can be observed between two molecules is
questions.explanation: Van der Waals forces are weak intermolecular attractions, much weaker than ionic or covalent bonds.

questions.stem: A consequence of global warming is
questions.explanation: Global warming melts ice caps and raises sea levels, leading to flooding.

questions.stem: Which of the following ions is acidic?
questions.explanation: The hydroxonium ion H3O+ is the species responsible for acidity in aqueous solution.

questions.stem: The structural component that makes detergent dissolve more quickly in water than soap is
questions.explanation: Synthetic detergents are sodium alkylbenzene sulphonates; the -SO3^- Na+ head is very soluble and forms no scum with hard water.

questions.stem: A liquid that will dissolve fat is
questions.explanation: Fats are non-polar and dissolve in non-polar organic solvents such as kerosene.

questions.stem: Farmlands affected by crude-oil spillage can be decontaminated by
options: pouring water on the affected area
burning off the oil from the area.
questions.explanation: Aerobic bacteria biodegrade the hydrocarbons (bioremediation).

questions.stem: A change in the temperature of a saturated solution disturbs the equilibrium between the
options: dissolved solute and the undissolved solute
questions.explanation: In a saturated solution there is a dynamic equilibrium between dissolved and undissolved solute; temperature changes the solubility.

questions.stem: If an equilibrium reaction has ΔH > 0, the reaction will proceed favourably in the forward direction at
questions.explanation: A positive ΔH means the forward reaction is endothermic, so raising the temperature favours it.

questions.stem: The commonest feature of reaction at the anode is that
questions.explanation: At the anode species lose electrons, i.e. oxidation always occurs there.

questions.stem: Which of the following will change when a catalyst is added to a chemical reaction?
options: The potential energy of the reactants
The potential energy of the products.
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy; ΔH and the energies of reactants and products are unchanged.

questions.stem: If Y is an oxidizing agent that reacts with a reducing agent, Z, which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: An oxidising agent gains electrons and is itself reduced.

questions.stem: When at equilibrium, which of the reactions below will shift to the right if the pressure is increased and the temperature is kept constant?
questions.explanation: Increased pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules; only in C does the forward reaction reduce the number (3 to 2).

questions.stem: In the electrolysis of a concentrated solution of sodium chloride using inert electrodes, which of the following ions are discharged at the cathode and anode respectively?
questions.explanation: H+ is preferentially discharged at the cathode; the high concentration of Cl- makes it discharged at the anode.

questions.stem: CO(g) + H2O(g) → CO2(g) + H2(g). From the reaction above, calculate the standard heat change if the standard enthalpies of formation of CO2(g), H2O(g) and CO(g) in kJ mol^-1 are –394, -242 and –110 respectively.
When sugar is dissolved in a tea, the reaction is always accompanied by

questions.stem: Which of the following is an electrolyte?
questions.explanation: Sodium acetate solution contains mobile ions and is decomposed by current; solid KOH has no mobile ions, alcohol is a non-electrolyte and mercury is a metallic conductor.

questions.topic: Metals of the first transition series
questions.stem: Metals of the transition series have special properties which are different from those of groups 1 and II elements because they have partially filled
questions.explanation: Transition metals have incompletely filled 3d orbitals, giving variable valency, coloured ions and catalytic activity.

questions.stem: Hydrogen can be displaced from a hot alkaline solution by
questions.explanation: Tin is amphoteric and reacts with hot concentrated alkali to form a stannate and liberate hydrogen.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true of sulphur (IV) oxide?
options: It forms tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid with water
It forms white precipitate with acidified barium chloride.
questions.explanation: SO2 dissolves in water to form trioxosulphate(IV) acid, so it is an acid anhydride.

questions.stem: The salt that will form a precipitate soluble in excess ammonia solution is
questions.explanation: Cu2+ gives a blue Cu(OH)2 precipitate which dissolves in excess NH3 to form the deep-blue tetraamminecopper(II) complex.

questions.stem: The metal that liberates hydrogen from cold water in bubbles only is
questions.explanation: Calcium reacts steadily with cold water giving bubbles of H2; Na and K react violently and Al does not react.

questions.stem: Chlorine gas turns a damp starch-iodide paper
questions.explanation: Chlorine displaces iodine from iodide; iodine forms a blue-black complex with starch.

questions.stem: The modern process of manufacturing steel from iron is by
questions.explanation: In the basic oxygen process oxygen is blown through molten pig iron to oxidise away excess carbon and impurities.

questions.stem: Ethene reacts with hydrogen bromide to give
questions.explanation: HBr adds across the double bond: CH2=CH2 + HBr → CH3CH2Br (bromoethane).

questions.stem: Carbohydrates are compounds containing carbon, hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates have the general formula Cx(H2O)y, e.g. glucose C6H12O6, with C : H : O = 1 : 2 : 1.

questions.stem: How many isomers does pentane have?
questions.explanation: C5H12 has three isomers: pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane.

questions.stem: The formula for ethyl butanoate is
questions.explanation: Butanoic acid is C3H7COOH; its ethyl ester is C3H7COOC2H5.

questions.stem: The type of reaction that is peculiar to benzene is
questions.explanation: The stable delocalised ring of benzene makes electrophilic substitution its characteristic reaction.

questions.stem: Ethanol reacts with excess acidified K2Cr2O7 to give
questions.explanation: With excess oxidant, ethanol is oxidised completely through ethanal to ethanoic acid.

questions.stem: A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen. If the molar mass of the compound is 180, find the molecular formula. [H = 1, C = 12, O = 16]
questions.explanation: C 3.33, H 6.7, O 3.33 gives empirical formula CH2O (mass 30); n = 180/30 = 6, so C6H12O6.

questions.stem: The process by which atoms are rearranged into different molecular structures in the petroleum refining process is referred to as
questions.explanation: Reforming rearranges straight-chain molecules into branched or cyclic/aromatic structures to raise octane number.

questions.stem: Which of the following is found in cotton?
questions.explanation: Cotton fibre is almost pure cellulose.

questions.stem: The principal constituent of natural gas is
questions.explanation: Natural gas is mainly methane.

questions.stem: In the electrolysis of brine, the anode is
questions.explanation: Industrially the anode used for brine is carbon (graphite), which resists attack by the chlorine liberated.

questions.stem: N2O4(g) ⇌ 2NO2(g). In the endothermic reaction above, more product formation will be favoured by
questions.explanation: The forward reaction increases the number of gas molecules (1 to 2), so lowering the pressure favours it.

questions.stem: The oxidation state of chlorine in HClO4 is

questions.explanation: Standard molar entropy increases with molar mass down the group (HF < HCl < HBr < HI), so HI is highest.

questions.explanation: Sulphur in SO2 is +4, intermediate between -2 and +6, so SO2 can be oxidised (reducing agent) or reduced (oxidising agent, e.g. with H2S).

questions.stem: Which of the following shows little or no net reaction when the volume of the system is decreased?
questions.explanation: In H2 + I2 ⇌ 2HI there are equal numbers of gas molecules on both sides, so a pressure (volume) change does not shift the equilibrium.

questions.stem: ZnO + CO → Zn + CO2. In the reaction above, zinc has been
questions.explanation: Zinc goes from +2 in ZnO to 0 in the metal: it gains electrons and is reduced.

questions.explanation: CaCO3 (100 g/mol): 2 g = 0.02 mol, giving 0.02 mol CO2 = 0.02 x 22400 = 448 cm3.

questions.stem: A chemical reaction is always associated with
options: a change in the nature of the reactants
a change in the volume of the reactants
an increase in the composition of one of the substances
questions.explanation: A chemical change always produces new substances.

questions.stem: When a solid substance disappears completely as a gas on heating, the substance is said to have undergone
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to vapour on heating.

questions.stem: If a solution contains 4.9 g of tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid, calculate the amount of copper (II) oxide that will react with it [Cu = 64, O = 16, S = 32, H = 1]
questions.explanation: CuO + H2SO4 → CuSO4 + H2O; 4.9/98 = 0.05 mol acid reacts with 0.05 mol CuO = 0.05 x 80 = 4.0 g.

questions.stem: Vulcanization involves the removal of
questions.explanation: Sulphur forms cross-links across the C=C double bonds of rubber, so double bonds are removed.

questions.stem: The alkyl group can be represented by the general formula
questions.explanation: An alkyl group is an alkane (CnH2n+2) minus one hydrogen atom: CnH2n+1.

questions.stem: C2H5OH(aq) + conc. H2SO4 at 180 °C → Y. In the reaction above, Y represents
questions.explanation: Excess concentrated H2SO4 at about 180 °C dehydrates ethanol to ethene.

questions.stem: In the production of soap, concentrated sodium chloride is added to
options: decrease the solubility of the soap
increase the solubility of the soap
questions.explanation: Salting out: brine lowers the solubility of soap so that it separates out of the mixture.

questions.stem: Oxyacetylene flame is used for iron-welding because it
options: evolves a lot of heat when burnt
dissociates to produce carbon (IV) oxide and oxygen
makes the iron metal solidify very quickly
combines with oxygen to give a pop sound.
questions.explanation: Ethyne burns in oxygen with a very hot flame (about 3000 °C), hot enough to melt iron.

questions.stem: Which of these reagents can confirm the presence of a triple bond?
questions.explanation: Ammoniacal copper(I) chloride gives a red precipitate with terminal alkynes; bromine and KMnO4 react with double bonds too.

questions.stem: CH3CH(CH3)CH(CH3)CH2CH2CH3. The IUPAC nomenclature of the compound above is
questions.explanation: The longest chain has six carbons with methyl groups on C-2 and C-3, numbering from the end nearer the branches.

questions.stem: An isomer of C5H12 is
questions.explanation: 2-methylbutane, CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH3, has formula C5H12; butane and 2-methylpropane are C4H10 and 2-ethylbutane would be C6H14.

questions.stem: Alkanol + Alkanoic acid ⇌ Ester + Water. The reverse reaction of the equation above is known as
questions.explanation: The reverse of esterification is the hydrolysis of the ester by water into acid and alcohol.

questions.stem: CH3COOH(g) → CH4(g) + CO2(g). The reaction above is
questions.explanation: Removal of CO2 from a carboxylic acid is decarboxylation.

questions.stem: A characteristic of the alkane family is
questions.explanation: Alkanes are saturated, so they react by substitution (e.g. with chlorine in light).

questions.stem: Pollution of underground water by metal ions is very likely in a soil that has high
questions.explanation: Acidic conditions dissolve metal compounds, releasing metal ions that leach into groundwater.

questions.stem: Which of these compounds is a normal salt?
questions.explanation: In Na2CO3 all the replaceable hydrogen of the acid has been replaced; the others are acid salts.

questions.stem: A carcinogenic substance is
questions.explanation: Inhaled asbestos fibres cause lung cancer and mesothelioma.

Hardness of water is caused by the presence of the ions of

questions.stem: It is difficult to achieve an orderly arrangement of the molecules of a gas because they
options: can collide with one another in the container
have little force of attraction between them
questions.explanation: Gas molecules have negligible intermolecular attraction, so they move freely and randomly.

questions.stem: Chlorine consisting of two isotopes of mass numbers 35 and 37 in the ratio 3:1 has an atomic mass of 35.5. Calculate the relative abundance of the isotope of mass number 37.

questions.stem: Carbon is tetravalent because
options: all the atomic orbitals of carbon hybridize
the electrons in all the orbitals of carbon are equivalent
the electrons in both the 2s and 2p orbitals are equivalent.
questions.explanation: One 2s electron is promoted and the 2s and three 2p orbitals hybridise (sp3) to give four equivalent bonding orbitals.

reducing a mixture of their metallic oxides
